entries.name: arch.unitroot.VarianceRatio
entries.summary: Variance Ratio test of a random walk.
keywords:
Variance Ratio test of a random walk.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data to test for a random walk.
lags : int, optional
    The number of periods to use in the multi-period variance, which is
    the numerator of the test statistic.  Must be at least 2.
trend : {"n", "c"}, optional
    "c" allows for a non-zero drift in the random walk, while "n" requires
    that the increments to y are mean 0. Not case sensitive.
debiased : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use a debiased version of the test. Only
    applicable if overlap is True.
robust : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use heteroskedasticity robust inference.
overlap : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use all overlapping blocks.  If
    False, the number of observations in y minus 1 must be an exact
    multiple of lags.  If this condition is not satisfied, some values at
    the end of y will be discarded, and are not included in nobs.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` is not an integer, `debiased`,
    `robust` or `overlap` is not a bool, or `trend` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` is less than 2, or `trend`
    is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `lags`. At least
    `lags` + 1 observations are needed (`lags` + 2 if `debiased`), or
    2 * `lags` if `overlap` is False. This is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of a VR is that the process is a random walk, possibly
plus drift.  Rejection of the null with a positive test statistic
indicates the presence of positive serial correlation in the time series.
See [1]_ for details about variance ratio testing.

References
----------
.. [1] Campbell, John Y., Lo, Andrew W. and MacKinlay, A. Craig. (1997) The
   Econometrics of Financial Markets. Princeton, NJ: Princeton University
   Press.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.ZivotAndrews
entries.summary: Zivot-Andrews structural-break unit-root test.
keywords:
Zivot-Andrews structural-break unit-root test.

The Zivot-Andrews test can be used to test for a unit root in a
univariate process in the presence of serial correlation and a
single structural break.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data series.
lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the ADF regression.  If omitted or None,
    `method` is used to automatically select the lag length with no more
    than `max_lags` lags included.
trend : {"c", "t", "ct"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "t" - Include a linear time trend
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend

trim : float, optional
    Percentage of series at begin/end to exclude from break-period
    calculation in range [0, 0.333]. The number of observations that are
    excluded, int(nobs * trim), must be larger than the number of lags, so
    that trim cannot be 0.
max_lags : int, optional
    The maximum number of lags to use when selecting lag length.
method : {"aic", "bic", "t-stat", "maic"}, optional
    The method to use when selecting the lag length. Not case sensitive.

    - "aic" - Select the minimum of the Akaike IC
    - "bic" - Select the minimum of the Schwarz/Bayesian IC
    - "t-stat" - Select the largest lag length for which the t-statistic
      of the last lag is significant, using a cut-off of 1.645 for the
      absolute value of the t-statistic
    - "maic" - Select the minimum of Ng and Perron's modified Akaike IC

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` or `max_lags` is not an
    integer, `trim` is not a real number, or `trend` or `method` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` or `max_lags` is
    negative, `trim` is not in [0, 1/3], or `trend` or `method` is not one of
    the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, `lags` or
    `max_lags`, or int(nobs * trim) is too small for `lags` and `trend`. This
    is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
H0 = unit root with a single structural break

Algorithm follows Baum (2004/2015) approximation to original
Zivot-Andrews method. Rather than performing an autolag regression at
each candidate break period (as per the original paper), a single
autolag regression is run up-front on the base model (constant + trend
with no dummies) to determine the best lag length. This lag length is
then used for all subsequent break-period regressions. This results in
significant run time reduction but also slightly more pessimistic test
statistics than the original Zivot-Andrews method.

No attempt has been made to characterize the size/power trade-off.

Based on the description in Zivot and Andrews [3]_. See [2]_ for
a general discussion of unit root tests. Code tested against Baum [1]_.

References
----------
.. [1] Baum, C.F. (2004). ZANDREWS: Stata module to calculate Zivot-Andrews
       unit root test in presence of structural break," Statistical Software
       Components S437301, Boston College Department of Economics, revised
       2015.

.. [2] Schwert, G.W. (1989). Tests for unit roots: A Monte Carlo
       investigation. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 7: 147-159.

.. [3] Zivot, E., and Andrews, D.W.K. (1992). Further evidence on the great
       crash, the oil-price shock, and the unit-root hypothesis. Journal of
       Business & Economic Studies, 10: 251-270.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.cointegration.DynamicOLS
entries.summary: Dynamic OLS (DOLS) cointegrating vector estimation.
keywords:
Dynamic OLS (DOLS) cointegrating vector estimation.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The left-hand-side variable in the cointegrating regression. It must be
    1-d and contain only finite values.
x : array_like
    The right-hand-side variables in the cointegrating regression. It must
    be 1-d or 2-d with the same number of rows as y, at least 1 column,
    the same index as y if both are pandas objects, and contain only finite
    values. The number of rows must be at least two more than the number of
    parameters in the cointegrating regression (the number of columns of x
    and the number of terms in trend).
trend : {"n", "c", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    Trend to include in the cointegrating regression. Not case sensitive.
    Trends are:

    * "n": No deterministic terms
    * "c": Constant
    * "ct": Constant and linear trend
    * "ctt": Constant, linear and quadratic trends

lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to include in the model.  If None, the optimal
    number of lags is chosen using method. It must be an integer between 0
    and nobs - 2.
leads : int, optional
    The number of leads to include in the model.  If None, the optimal
    number of leads is chosen using method. It must be an integer between 0
    and nobs - 2.
common : bool, optional
    Flag indicating that lags and leads should be restricted to the same
    value. When common is True, lags must equal leads and max_lag must
    equal max_lead.
max_lag : int, optional
    The maximum lag to consider. See Notes for value used when None. It
    must be an integer between 0 and nobs - 2.
max_lead : int, optional
    The maximum lead to consider. See Notes for value used when None. It
    must be an integer between 0 and nobs - 2.
method : {"aic", "bic", "hqic"}, optional
    The method used to select lag length when lags or leads is None. Not
    case sensitive.

    * "aic" - Akaike Information Criterion
    * "hqic" - Hannan-Quinn Information Criterion
    * "bic" - Schwartz/Bayesian Information Criterion

Raises
------
TypeError
    If y or x cannot be converted to float64, lags, leads, max_lag or
    max_lead is not an integer or None, common is not a bool, or trend or
    method is not a string.
ValueError
    If y or x contains NaN or inf, does not have the required dimensions, the
    same number of rows or the same index, or has too few rows. Also if lags,
    leads, max_lag or max_lead is not between 0 and nobs - 2, if common is
    True and lags and leads (or max_lag and max_lead) differ, if the sample
    that remains after the differences, lags and leads is not larger than
    the number of parameters of the smallest model that is estimated, or if
    trend or method is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If y is constant. This is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The cointegrating vector is estimated from the regression

.. math ::

   Y_t = D_t \delta + X_t \beta + \Delta X_{t} \gamma
         + \sum_{i=1}^p \Delta X_{t-i} \kappa_i
         + \sum _{j=1}^q \Delta X_{t+j} \lambda_j + \epsilon_t

where p is the lag length and q is the lead length.  :math:`D_t` is a
vector containing the deterministic terms, if any. All specifications
include the contemporaneous difference :math:`\Delta X_{t}`.

When lag lengths are not provided, the optimal lag length is chosen to
minimize an Information Criterion of the form

.. math::

    \ln\left(\hat{\sigma}^2\right) + k\frac{c}{T}

where c is 2 for Akaike, :math:`2\ln\ln T` for Hannan-Quinn and
:math:`\ln T` for Schwartz/Bayesian.

See [1]_ and [2]_ for further details.

References
----------
.. [1] Saikkonen, P. (1992). Estimation and testing of cointegrated
   systems by an autoregressive approximation. Econometric theory,
   8(1), 1-27.
.. [2] Stock, J. H., & Watson, M. W. (1993). A simple estimator of
   cointegrating vectors in higher order integrated systems.
   Econometrica: Journal of the Econometric Society, 783-820.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.cointegration.engle_granger
entries.summary: Test for cointegration within a set of time series.
keywords:
Test for cointegration within a set of time series.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The left-hand-side variable in the cointegrating regression. It must be
    1-d and contain only finite values.
x : array_like
    The right-hand-side variables in the cointegrating regression. It must
    be 1-d or 2-d with the same number of rows as y, between 1 and 11 columns,
    the same index as y if both are pandas objects, and contain only finite
    values. The number of rows must be at least two more than the number of
    parameters in the cointegrating regression (the number of columns of x
    and the number of terms in trend).
trend : {"n", "c", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    Trend to include in the cointegrating regression. Not case sensitive.
    Trends are:

    * "n": No deterministic terms
    * "c": Constant
    * "ct": Constant and linear trend
    * "ctt": Constant, linear and quadratic trends

lags : int, optional
    The number of lagged differences to include in the Augmented
    Dickey-Fuller test used on the residuals of the cointegrating
    regression. It must be a non-negative integer. If None, the number of
    lags is selected using ``method``.
max_lags : int, optional
    The maximum number of lags to consider when using automatic
    lag-length in the Augmented Dickey-Fuller regression. It must be an
    integer between 0 and nobs - 2.
method : {"aic", "bic", "t-stat", "maic"}, optional
    The method used to select the number of lags included in the
    Augmented Dickey-Fuller regression. Not case sensitive.

    * "aic": Select the minimum of the Akaike IC
    * "bic": Select the minimum of the Schwarz/Bayesian IC
    * "t-stat": Select the largest lag length for which the t-statistic
      of the last lag is significant, using a cut-off of 1.645 for the
      absolute value of the t-statistic
    * "maic": Select the minimum of Ng and Perron's modified Akaike IC

low_memory : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to use the low memory implementation of the
    lag selection algorithm in the Augmented Dickey-Fuller regression.
    If None, the algorithm is selected automatically. See
    :class:`arch.unitroot.ADF`.

Returns
-------
EngleGrangerTestResults
    Results of the Engle-Granger test.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If y or x cannot be converted to float64, lags or max_lags is not an
    integer or None, low_memory is not a bool or None, or trend or method is
    not a string.
ValueError
    If y or x contains NaN or inf, does not have the required dimensions, the
    same number of rows or the same index, or has too few rows. Also if x has
    more than 11 columns, lags is negative, max_lags is not between 0 and
    nobs - 2, or trend or method is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant, or the Augmented Dickey-Fuller regression of the
    residual cannot be estimated with the lags requested. This is also a
    ValueError.

See Also
--------
arch.unitroot.ADF
    Augmented Dickey-Fuller testing.
arch.unitroot.PhillipsPerron
    Phillips & Perron's unit root test.
arch.unitroot.cointegration.phillips_ouliaris
    Phillips-Ouliaris tests of cointegration.

Notes
-----
The model estimated is

.. math::

   Y_t = X_t \beta + D_t \gamma + \epsilon_t

where :math:`Z_t = [Y_t,X_t]` is being tested for cointegration.
:math:`D_t` is a set of deterministic terms that may include a
constant, a time trend or a quadratic time trend.

The null hypothesis is that the series are not cointegrated.

The test is implemented as an ADF of the estimated residuals from the
cross-sectional regression using a set of critical values that is
determined by the number of assumed stochastic trends when the null
hypothesis is true.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.cointegration.phillips_ouliaris
entries.summary: Test for cointegration within a set of time series.
keywords:
Test for cointegration within a set of time series.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The left-hand-side variable in the cointegrating regression. It must be
    1-d and contain only finite values.
x : array_like
    The right-hand-side variables in the cointegrating regression. It must
    be 1-d or 2-d with the same number of rows as y, between 1 and 12 columns,
    the same index as y if both are pandas objects, and contain only finite
    values. The number of rows must be at least two more than the number of
    parameters in the cointegrating regression (the number of columns of x
    and the number of terms in trend).
trend : {"n", "c", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    Trend to include in the cointegrating regression. Not case sensitive.
    Trends are:

    * "n": No deterministic terms
    * "c": Constant
    * "ct": Constant and linear trend
    * "ctt": Constant, linear and quadratic trends

test_type : {"za", "zt", "pu", "pz"}, optional
    The test statistic to compute. Not case sensitive. Supported options are:

    * "za": The Zα test based on the debiased AR(1) coefficient.
    * "zt": The Zt test based on the t-statistic from an AR(1).
    * "pu": The Pᵤ variance-ratio test.
    * "pz": The Pz test of the trace of the product of an estimate of the
      long-run residual variance and the inner-product of the data.

    See the notes for details on the test.
kernel : str, optional
    The string name of any known kernel-based long-run
    covariance estimator. Common choices are "bartlett" for the
    Bartlett kernel (Newey-West), "parzen" for the Parzen kernel
    and "quadratic-spectral" for the Quadratic Spectral kernel. Not case
    sensitive.
bandwidth : float, optional
    The bandwidth to use. It must be a finite non-negative number. If not
    provided, the optimal bandwidth is estimated from the data. Setting the
    bandwidth to 0 produces White's covariance estimator.
force_int : bool, optional
    Whether to force the estimated optimal bandwidth to be an integer.
bandwidth_method : {"newey-west", "andrews"}, optional
    The method used to estimate the bandwidth when bandwidth is None.
    "newey-west" uses the nonparametric estimate of Newey and West (1994)
    and "andrews" uses the AR(1) plug-in estimate of Andrews (1991), see
    ``opt_bandwidth`` of the kernel estimators. Not case sensitive, and
    hyphens and underscores are ignored as in the names of kernels.
    Ignored if bandwidth is provided.

Returns
-------
PhillipsOuliarisTestResults
    Results of the Phillips-Ouliaris test.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If y or x cannot be converted to float64, bandwidth is not a real number
    or None, force_int is not a bool, or trend, test_type, kernel or
    bandwidth_method is not a string.
ValueError
    If y or x contains NaN or inf, does not have the required dimensions, the
    same number of rows or the same index, or has too few rows. Also if x has
    more than 12 columns, bandwidth is negative, NaN or inf, trend,
    test_type, kernel or bandwidth_method is not one of the options, or
    bandwidth_method is "andrews" and the AR(1) cannot be fitted to the
    residuals.
InfeasibleTestException
    If y is constant. This is also a ``ValueError``.

See Also
--------
arch.unitroot.ADF
    Augmented Dickey-Fuller testing.
arch.unitroot.PhillipsPerron
    Phillips & Perron's unit root test.
arch.unitroot.cointegration.engle_granger
    Engle & Granger's cointegration test.

Notes
-----
Supports 4 distinct tests.

Define the cross-sectional regression

.. math::

   y_t = x_t \beta + d_t \gamma + u_t

where :math:`d_t` are any included deterministic terms. Let
:math:`\hat{u}_t = y_t - x_t \hat{\beta} + d_t \hat{\gamma}`.

The Zα and Zt statistics are defined as

.. math::

   \hat{Z}_\alpha & = T \times z \\
   \hat{Z}_t & =  \frac{\hat{\sigma}_u}{\hat{\omega}^2} \times \sqrt{T} z \\
   z & = (\hat{\alpha} - 1) - \hat{\omega}^2_1 / \hat{\sigma}^2_u

where :math:`\hat{\sigma}^2_u=T^{-1}\sum_{t=2}^T \hat{u}_t^2`,
:math:`\hat{\omega}^2_1` is an estimate of the one-sided strict
autocovariance, and :math:`\hat{\omega}^2` is an estimate of the long-run
variance of the process.

The :math:`\hat{P}_u` variance-ratio statistic is defined as

.. math::

   \hat{P}_u = \frac{\hat{\omega}_{11\cdot2}}{\tilde{\sigma}^2_u}

where :math:`\tilde{\sigma}^2_u=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T \hat{u}_t^2` and

.. math::

   \hat{\omega}_{11\cdot 2} = \hat{\omega}_{11}
                             - \hat{\omega}'_{21} \hat{\Omega}_{22}^{-1}
                               \hat{\omega}_{21}

and

.. math::

   \hat{\Omega}=\left[\begin{array}{cc} \hat{\omega}_{11} & \hat{\omega}'_{21}\\
                                        \hat{\omega}_{21} & \hat{\Omega}_{22}
                \end{array}\right]

is an estimate of the long-run covariance of :math:`\xi_t`, the residuals
from an VAR(1) on :math:`z_t=[y_t,z_t]` that includes and trends included
in the test.

.. math::

   z_t = \Phi z_{t-1} + \xi_\tau

The final test statistic is defined

.. math::

   \hat{P}_z = T \times \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\Omega} M_{zz}^{-1})

where :math:`M_{zz} = \sum_{t=1}^T \tilde{z}'_t \tilde{z}_t`,
:math:`\tilde{z}_t` is the vector of data :math:`z_t=[y_t,x_t]` detrended
using any trend terms included in the test,
:math:`\tilde{z}_t = z_t - d_t \hat{\kappa}` and :math:`\hat{\Omega}` is
defined above.

The specification of the :math:`\hat{P}_z` test statistic when trend is "n"
differs from the expression in [1]_. We recenter :math:`z_t` by subtracting
the first observation, so that :math:`\tilde{z}_t = z_t - z_1`. This is
needed to ensure that the initial value does not affect the distribution
under the null. When the trend is anything other than "n", this step is not
needed and the test statistics is identical whether the first observation
is subtracted or not.

References
----------
.. [1] Phillips, P. C., & Ouliaris, S. (1990). Asymptotic properties of
   residual based tests for cointegration. Econometrica: Journal of the
   Econometric Society, 165-193.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.ADF
entries.summary: Augmented Dickey-Fuller unit root test.
keywords:
Augmented Dickey-Fuller unit root test.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data to test for a unit root.
lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the ADF regression.  If omitted or None,
    `method` is used to automatically select the lag length with no more
    than `max_lags` lags included.
trend : {"n", "c", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "n" - No trend components
    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend
    - "ctt" - Include a constant and linear and quadratic time trends

max_lags : int, optional
    The maximum number of lags to use when selecting lag length. If
    omitted or None, the maximum number of lags is 12 * (nobs/100) ** (1/4),
    rounded up, reduced when needed in short samples.
method : {"aic", "bic", "t-stat", "maic"}, optional
    The method to use when selecting the lag length. Not case sensitive.

    - "aic" - Select the minimum of the Akaike IC
    - "bic" - Select the minimum of the Schwarz/Bayesian IC
    - "t-stat" - Select the largest lag length for which the t-statistic
      of the last lag is significant, using a cut-off of 1.645 for the
      absolute value of the t-statistic
    - "maic" - Select the minimum of Ng and Perron's modified Akaike IC ([5]_)

low_memory : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to use a low memory implementation of the
    lag selection algorithm. The low memory algorithm is slower than
    the standard algorithm but will use 2-4% of the memory required for
    the standard algorithm. This options allows automatic lag selection
    to be used in very long time series. If None, the low memory algorithm
    is used when the series has more than 100,000 observations.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` or `max_lags` is not an
    integer, `low_memory` is not a bool or None, or `trend` or `method` is not
    a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` or `max_lags` is
    negative, or `trend` or `method` is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, or `lags` or
    `max_lags` is larger than the observations can support. A regression with
    `lags` lags needs at least 3 + 2 * `lags` + the number of trend terms
    observations. This is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of the Augmented Dickey-Fuller is that there is a unit
root, with the alternative that there is no unit root. If the pvalue is
above a critical size, then the null cannot be rejected and the series
appears to be a unit root.

The p-values are from an approximation of the asymptotic distribution of the
statistic that follows the methodology of MacKinnon (1994), and are a smooth
and increasing function of the statistic. The critical values are from
response surface regressions that follow the methodology of MacKinnon (2010),
and depend on the number of observations. Both are fit to the same new
simulations, and the p-values of the asymptotic critical values are 1%, 5% and
10%.
If the p-value is close to significant, then the critical values should be
used to judge whether to reject the null.

The autolag option and maxlag for it are described in Greene [1]_.
See Hamilton [2]_ for more on ADF tests. Critical value simulation based
on MacKinnon [3]_ and [4]_.

References
----------
.. [1] Greene, W. H. 2011. Econometric Analysis. Prentice Hall: Upper
   Saddle River, New Jersey.

.. [2] Hamilton, J. D. 1994. Time Series Analysis. Princeton: Princeton
   University Press.

.. [3] MacKinnon, J.G. 1994.  "Approximate asymptotic distribution
   functions for unit-root and cointegration tests.  `Journal of
   Business and Economic Statistics` 12, 167-76.

.. [4] MacKinnon, J.G. 2010. "Critical Values for Cointegration Tests."
   Queen's University, Dept of Economics, Working Papers.  Available at
   https://ideas.repec.org/p/qed/wpaper/1227.html
.. [5] Ng, S., and P. Perron. 2001. "Lag Length Selection and the
   Construction of Unit Root Tests with Good Size and Power."
   Econometrica 69, 1519-1554.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.DFGLS
entries.summary: Elliott, Rothenberg and Stock's ([ers]_) GLS detrended Dickey-Fuller.
keywords:
Elliott, Rothenberg and Stock's ([ers]_) GLS detrended Dickey-Fuller.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data to test for a unit root.
lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the ADF regression.  If omitted or None,
    `method` is used to automatically select the lag length with no more
    than `max_lags` lags included.
trend : {"c", "ct"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend

max_lags : int, optional
    The maximum number of lags to use when selecting lag length. When using
    automatic lag length selection, the lag is selected using OLS
    detrending rather than GLS detrending ([pq]_). If omitted or None,
    the maximum number of lags is 12 * (nobs/100) ** (1/4), rounded up,
    reduced when needed in short samples.
method : {"aic", "bic", "t-stat", "maic"}, optional
    The method to use when selecting the lag length. Not case sensitive.

    - "aic" - Select the minimum of the Akaike IC
    - "bic" - Select the minimum of the Schwarz/Bayesian IC
    - "t-stat" - Select the largest lag length for which the t-statistic
      of the last lag is significant, using a cut-off of 1.645 for the
      absolute value of the t-statistic
    - "maic" - Select the minimum of Ng and Perron's modified Akaike IC ([np]_)

low_memory : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to use a low memory implementation of the
    lag selection algorithm. The low memory algorithm is slower than
    the standard algorithm but will use 2-4% of the memory required for
    the standard algorithm. This options allows automatic lag selection
    to be used in very long time series. If None, the low memory algorithm
    is used when the series has at least 100,000 observations.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` or `max_lags` is not an
    integer, `low_memory` is not a bool or None, or `trend` or `method` is not
    a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` or `max_lags` is
    negative, or `trend` or `method` is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, or `lags` or
    `max_lags` is larger than the observations can support. A regression with
    `lags` lags needs at least 3 + 2 * `lags` observations. This is also a
    ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of the Dickey-Fuller GLS is that there is a unit
root, with the alternative that there is no unit root. If the pvalue is
above a critical size, then the null cannot be rejected and the series
appears to be a unit root.

DFGLS differs from the ADF test in that an initial GLS detrending step
is used before a trend-less ADF regression is run.

Critical values and p-values when trend is "c" are identical to
the ADF.  When trend is set to "ct", they are from novel simulations.

References
----------
.. [ers] Elliott, G. R., T. J. Rothenberg, and J. H. Stock. 1996. Efficient
       tests for an autoregressive unit root. Econometrica 64: 813-836
.. [pq] Perron, P., & Qu, Z. (2007). A simple modification to improve the
       finite sample properties of Ng and Perron's unit root tests.
       Economics letters, 94(1), 12-19.
.. [np] Ng, S., and P. Perron. 2001. "Lag Length Selection and the
       Construction of Unit Root Tests with Good Size and Power."
       Econometrica 69, 1519-1554.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.KPSS
entries.summary: Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt and Shin (KPSS) stationarity test.
keywords:
Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt and Shin (KPSS) stationarity test.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data to test for stationarity.
lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the Newey-West estimator of the long-run
    covariance.  If omitted or None, the number of lags is calculated
    with the data-dependent method of Hobijn et al. (1998). See also
    Andrews (1991), Newey & West (1994), and Schwert (1989).
    Set lags=-1 to use the old method that only depends on the sample
    size, 12 * (nobs/100) ** (1/4).
trend : {"c", "ct"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` is not an integer or None,
    or `trend` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` is less than -1, or
    `trend` is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, or `lags`
    (the number from the rule 12 * (nobs/100) ** (1/4) if it is -1) is
    larger than the number of observations in y. This is also a
    ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of the KPSS test is that the series is weakly
stationary and the alternative is that it is non-stationary.
If the p-value is above a critical size, then the null cannot be
rejected and the series appears stationary.

The p-values and critical values were computed using an extensive
simulation based on 100,000,000 replications using series with 2,000
observations. See [3]_ for the initial description of the KPSS test.
Further details are available in [2]_ and [5]_. Details about the long-run
covariance estimation can be found in [1]_ and [4]_.

References
----------
.. [1] Andrews, D.W.K. (1991). "Heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation
       consistent covariance matrix estimation". Econometrica, 59: 817-858.

.. [2] Hobijn, B., Frances, B.H., & Ooms, M. (2004). Generalizations
       of the KPSS-test for stationarity. Statistica Neerlandica, 52: 483-502.

.. [3] Kwiatkowski, D.; Phillips, P. C. B.; Schmidt, P.; Shin, Y. (1992).
       "Testing the null hypothesis of stationarity against the alternative of
       a unit root". Journal of Econometrics 54 (1-3), 159-178

.. [4] Newey, W.K., & West, K.D. (1994). "Automatic lag selection in
       covariance matrix estimation". Review of Economic Studies, 61: 631-653.

.. [5] Schwert, G. W. (1989). "Tests for unit roots: A Monte Carlo
       investigation". Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 7 (2):
       147-159.

lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the Newey-West estimator of the long-run
    covariance.  If omitted or None, the lag length is set automatically to
    12 * (nobs/100) ** (1/4), rounded up.
trend : {"n", "c", "ct"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "n" - No trend components
    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend

test_type : {"tau", "rho"}, optional
    The test to use when computing the test statistic. Not case sensitive.
    "tau" is based on the t-stat and "rho" uses a test based on nobs times
    the re-centered regression coefficient.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` is not an integer, or
    `trend` or `test_type` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` is negative, or `trend`
    or `test_type` is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, or `lags`
    (the default number of lags if it is None) is larger than the number of
    observations in y minus 1. This is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of the Phillips-Perron (PP) test is that there is a
unit root, with the alternative that there is no unit root. If the pvalue
is above a critical size, then the null cannot be rejected and the series
appears to be a unit root.

Unlike the ADF test, the regression estimated includes only one lag of
the dependent variable, in addition to trend terms. Any serial
correlation in the regression errors is accounted for using a long-run
variance estimator (currently Newey-West).

See Philips and Perron for details [3]_. See Hamilton [1]_ for more on
PP tests. Newey and West contains information about long-run variance
estimation [2]_. The p-values are obtained through regression surface
approximation using the methodology of MacKinnon [4]_ and [5]_, only
using many more simulations.

If the p-value is close to significant, then the critical values should be
used to judge whether to reject the null.

References
----------
.. [1] Hamilton, J. D. 1994. Time Series Analysis. Princeton: Princeton
       University Press.

.. [2] Newey, W. K., and K. D. West. 1987. "A simple, positive
       semidefinite, heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent covariance
       matrix". Econometrica 55, 703-708.

.. [3] Phillips, P. C. B., and P. Perron. 1988. "Testing for a unit root in
       time series regression". Biometrika 75, 335-346.

.. [4] MacKinnon, J.G. 1994.  "Approximate asymptotic distribution
       functions for unit-root and cointegration tests".  Journal of
       Business and  Economic Statistics. 12, 167-76.

.. [5] MacKinnon, J.G. 2010. "Critical Values for Cointegration Tests."
       Queen's University, Dept of Economics, Working Papers.  Available at
       https://ideas.repec.org/p/qed/wpaper/1227.html

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.VarianceRatio
entries.summary: Variance Ratio test of a random walk.
keywords:
Variance Ratio test of a random walk.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data to test for a random walk.
lags : int, optional
    The number of periods to use in the multi-period variance, which is
    the numerator of the test statistic.  Must be at least 2.
trend : {"n", "c"}, optional
    "c" allows for a non-zero drift in the random walk, while "n" requires
    that the increments to y are mean 0. Not case sensitive.
debiased : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use a debiased version of the test. Only
    applicable if overlap is True.
robust : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use heteroskedasticity robust inference.
overlap : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to use all overlapping blocks.  If
    False, the number of observations in y minus 1 must be an exact
    multiple of lags.  If this condition is not satisfied, some values at
    the end of y will be discarded, and are not included in nobs.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` is not an integer, `debiased`,
    `robust` or `overlap` is not a bool, or `trend` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` is less than 2, or `trend`
    is not one of the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `lags`. At least
    `lags` + 1 observations are needed (`lags` + 2 if `debiased`), or
    2 * `lags` if `overlap` is False. This is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
The null hypothesis of a VR is that the process is a random walk, possibly
plus drift.  Rejection of the null with a positive test statistic
indicates the presence of positive serial correlation in the time series.
See [1]_ for details about variance ratio testing.

References
----------
.. [1] Campbell, John Y., Lo, Andrew W. and MacKinlay, A. Craig. (1997) The
   Econometrics of Financial Markets. Princeton, NJ: Princeton University
   Press.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.ZivotAndrews
entries.summary: Zivot-Andrews structural-break unit-root test.
keywords:
Zivot-Andrews structural-break unit-root test.

The Zivot-Andrews test can be used to test for a unit root in a
univariate process in the presence of serial correlation and a
single structural break.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    The data series.
lags : int, optional
    The number of lags to use in the ADF regression.  If omitted or None,
    `method` is used to automatically select the lag length with no more
    than `max_lags` lags included.
trend : {"c", "t", "ct"}, optional
    The trend component to include in the test. Not case sensitive.

    - "c" - Include a constant
    - "t" - Include a linear time trend
    - "ct" - Include a constant and linear time trend

trim : float, optional
    Percentage of series at begin/end to exclude from break-period
    calculation in range [0, 0.333]. The number of observations that are
    excluded, int(nobs * trim), must be larger than the number of lags, so
    that trim cannot be 0.
max_lags : int, optional
    The maximum number of lags to use when selecting lag length.
method : {"aic", "bic", "t-stat", "maic"}, optional
    The method to use when selecting the lag length. Not case sensitive.

    - "aic" - Select the minimum of the Akaike IC
    - "bic" - Select the minimum of the Schwarz/Bayesian IC
    - "t-stat" - Select the largest lag length for which the t-statistic
      of the last lag is significant, using a cut-off of 1.645 for the
      absolute value of the t-statistic
    - "maic" - Select the minimum of Ng and Perron's modified Akaike IC

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `y` cannot be converted to numbers, `lags` or `max_lags` is not an
    integer, `trim` is not a real number, or `trend` or `method` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `y` is not 1-d or contains NaN or inf, `lags` or `max_lags` is
    negative, `trim` is not in [0, 1/3], or `trend` or `method` is not one of
    the options.
InfeasibleTestException
    If `y` is constant or has too few observations for `trend`, `lags` or
    `max_lags`, or int(nobs * trim) is too small for `lags` and `trend`. This
    is also a ``ValueError``.

Notes
-----
H0 = unit root with a single structural break

Algorithm follows Baum (2004/2015) approximation to original
Zivot-Andrews method. Rather than performing an autolag regression at
each candidate break period (as per the original paper), a single
autolag regression is run up-front on the base model (constant + trend
with no dummies) to determine the best lag length. This lag length is
then used for all subsequent break-period regressions. This results in
significant run time reduction but also slightly more pessimistic test
statistics than the original Zivot-Andrews method.

No attempt has been made to characterize the size/power trade-off.

Based on the description in Zivot and Andrews [3]_. See [2]_ for
a general discussion of unit root tests. Code tested against Baum [1]_.

References
----------
.. [1] Baum, C.F. (2004). ZANDREWS: Stata module to calculate Zivot-Andrews
       unit root test in presence of structural break," Statistical Software
       Components S437301, Boston College Department of Economics, revised
       2015.

.. [2] Schwert, G.W. (1989). Tests for unit roots: A Monte Carlo
       investigation. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 7: 147-159.

.. [3] Zivot, E., and Andrews, D.W.K. (1992). Further evidence on the great
       crash, the oil-price shock, and the unit-root hypothesis. Journal of
       Business & Economic Studies, 10: 251-270.

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.mackinnoncrit
entries.summary: Return the critical values for cointegrating and the ADF test.
keywords:
Return the critical values for cointegrating and the ADF test.

The critical values are from response surface regressions that follow the
methodology of MacKinnon (2010), and depend on the number of observations.

Parameters
----------
num_unit_roots : int, optional
    The number of series of I(1) series for which the null of
    non-cointegration is being tested, from 1 to 12.  For the ADF test,
    N = 1. Values larger than 1 are only available when `dist_type` is
    "adf-t" and `regression` is not "n".
regression : {"c", "ct", "ctt", "n"}, optional
    Following MacKinnon (1996), these stand for the type of regression run.
    "c" for constant and no trend, "ct" for constant with a linear trend,
    "ctt" for constant with a linear and quadratic trend, and "n" for
    no constant. Not case sensitive.
nobs : int or float, optional
    This is the sample size, the number of observations in the regression of
    the test, which must be positive.  If the sample size is numpy.inf, then
    the asymptotic critical values are returned.
dist_type : {"adf-t", "adf-z", "dfgls"}, optional
    Type of test statistic. Not case sensitive.

Returns
-------
crit_vals : ndarray
    Three critical values corresponding to 1%, 5% and 10% cut-offs.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `num_unit_roots` is not an integer, `nobs` is not a real number or
    `regression` or `dist_type` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `num_unit_roots` is not between 1 and 12 (1 if `regression` is "n"),
    `nobs` is not positive or is NaN, `regression` or `dist_type` is not one of
    the options, or `num_unit_roots` is larger than 1 when `dist_type` is not
    "adf-t".

Notes
-----
The values for the ADF t-test with one unit root and for the ADF z-test are fit
to the same simulations as the p-values of mackinnonp, and the p-values of the
asymptotic critical values are 1%, 5% and 10%. The values for the DFGLS test
are also fit to new simulations. The values for the ADF t-test with more than
one unit root are from MacKinnon (2010).

References
----------
MacKinnon, J.G. 1994  "Approximate Asymptotic Distribution Functions for
    Unit-Root and Cointegration Tests." Journal of Business & Economics
    Statistics, 12.2, 167-76.
MacKinnon, J.G. 2010.  "Critical Values for Cointegration Tests."
    Queen's University, Dept of Economics Working Papers 1227.
    https://ideas.repec.org/p/qed/wpaper/1227.html

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.mackinnonp
entries.summary: Return MacKinnon's approximate p-value for test stat.
keywords:
Return MacKinnon's approximate p-value for test stat.

Parameters
----------
stat : float
    "T-value" from an Augmented Dickey-Fuller or DFGLS regression. It can be
    inf or -inf, but not NaN.
regression : {"c", "n", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    This is the method of regression that was used.  Following MacKinnon's
    notation, this can be "c" for constant, "n" for no constant, "ct" for
    constant and trend, and "ctt" for constant, trend, and trend-squared. Not
    case sensitive.
num_unit_roots : int, optional
    The number of series believed to be I(1), from 1 to 6.  For
    (Augmented) Dickey-Fuller N = 1. Values larger than 1 are only available
    when `dist_type` is "adf-t".
dist_type : {"adf-t", "adf-z", "dfgls"}, optional
    The test type to use when computing p-values.  Not case sensitive.
    Options include

    - "adf-t" - ADF t-stat based test
    - "adf-z" - ADF z test
    - "dfgls" - GLS detrended Dickey Fuller

Returns
-------
p-value : float
    The approximate asymptotic p-value of the statistic.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If `stat` is not a real number, `num_unit_roots` is not an integer or
    `regression` or `dist_type` is not a str.
ValueError
    If `stat` is NaN, `num_unit_roots` is not between 1 and 6, `regression` or
    `dist_type` is not one of the options, or `num_unit_roots` is larger than 1
    when `dist_type` is not "adf-t".

Notes
-----
The values for the ADF t-test with one unit root, the ADF z-test and the DFGLS
test are fit to new simulations following the methodology of MacKinnon (1994),
and are smooth and increasing functions of the statistic. The values for the ADF
t-test with more than one unit root are from MacKinnon (1994).

References
----------
MacKinnon, J.G. 1994  "Approximate Asymptotic Distribution Functions for
    Unit-Root and Cointegration Tests." Journal of Business & Economics
    Statistics, 12.2, 167-76.

entries.name: arch.univariate.APARCH
entries.summary: Asymmetric Power ARCH (APARCH) volatility process.
keywords:
Asymmetric Power ARCH (APARCH) volatility process.

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must satisfy p>=o and be positive.
o : int, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must satisfy o<=p and be
    non-negative.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be
    non-negative.
delta : float, optional
    Value to use for a fixed delta in the APARCH model. If
    not provided, the value of delta is jointly estimated
    with other model parameters. User provided delta is restricted
    to lie in (0.05, 4.0).
common_asym : bool, optional
    Restrict all asymmetry terms to share the same asymmetry
    parameter. If False (default), then there are no restrictions
    on the ``o`` asymmetry parameters.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer, ``delta`` is not a real number
    or None, or ``common_asym`` is not a bool.
ValueError
    If ``p`` is smaller than 1, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, ``o`` is larger than
    ``p``, or ``delta`` is NaN, inf or not in (0.05, 4.0).

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{\delta}=\omega
    +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}
    \left(\left|\epsilon_{t-i}\right|
    -\gamma_{i}I_{[o\geq i]}\epsilon_{t-i}\right)^{\delta}
    +\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\sigma_{t-k}^{\delta}

If ``common_asym`` is ``True``, then all of :math:`\gamma_i`
are restricted to have a common value.

entries.name: arch.univariate.ARCHInMean
entries.summary: (G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation.
keywords:
(G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable.
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Array with nobs rows and k columns containing exogenous regressors.  Must
    contain only finite values.
lags : int or array_like, optional
    Description of lag structure of the AR.  Scalar included all lags
    between 1 and the value.  A 1-d array includes the AR lags lags[0],
    lags[1], ...  The lags must be integers (2.5, 5.0 and True are not
    accepted). A scalar must be at least 0, and the values of an array at
    least 1.
constant : bool, optional
    Flag whether the model should include a constant.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.  Must be a non-negative
    integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model. ``volatility.updateable`` must
    return ``True``.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.
form : {"log", "vol", "var"}, int or float, optional
    The form of the conditional variance that appears in the mean equation. The
    string names use the log of the conditional variance ("log"), the square-root
    of the conditional variance ("vol") or the conditional variance. When
    specified using a float, interpreted as :math:`\sigma_t^{form}` so that
    1 is equivalent to "vol" and 2 is equivalent to "var". When using a number,
    must be finite and different from 0.  The strings are not case sensitive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool
    (``rescale`` can also be None), if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not
    an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`, or if ``x`` cannot be
    converted to numbers, or if ``form`` is not a string or a number.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is negative, empty or in an unsupported format, if the largest lag
    is not smaller than the number of observations, if ``hold_back`` is negative,
    if ``form`` is a string other than "log", "vol" or "var" or is not finite or
    is 0, or if ``x`` contains NaN or inf or does not have a row for each
    observation of ``y``.

Notes
-----
The (G)arch-in-mean model with exogenous regressors (-X)  is described by

.. math::

    y_t = \mu + \kappa f(\sigma^2_t)+ \sum_{i=1}^p \phi_{L_{i}} y_{t-L_{i}}
          + \gamma' x_t +  \epsilon_t

where :math:`f(\cdot)` is the function specified by ``form``.

entries.name: arch.univariate.EGARCH
entries.summary: EGARCH model estimation.
keywords:
EGARCH model estimation.

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
o : int, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be
    non-negative.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, or ``p`` and ``o`` are both 0.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \ln\sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega
    +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}
    \left(\left|e_{t-i}\right|-\sqrt{2/\pi}\right)
    +\sum_{j=1}^{o}\gamma_{j} e_{t-j}
    +\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\ln\sigma_{t-k}^{2}

where :math:`e_{t}=\epsilon_{t}/\sigma_{t}`.

entries.name: arch.univariate.FIAPARCH
entries.summary: Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process.
keywords:
Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process.

Parameters
----------
p : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation.
o : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation.
q : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance.
delta : float, optional
    Value to use for a fixed delta in the model. If not provided,
    the value of delta is jointly estimated with other model parameters.
    User provided delta is restricted to lie in (0.05, 4.0).
truncation : int, optional
    Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation.
    Default is 1000. Must be positive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o``, ``q`` or ``truncation`` is not an integer, or ``delta`` is
    not a real number or None.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not 0 or 1, ``truncation`` is smaller than 1, or
    ``delta`` is NaN, inf or not in (0.05, 4.0).

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_t^{\delta} = \omega
    + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L)(1-L)^d]
    (|\epsilon_{t}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t})^{\delta}
    + \beta \sigma_{t-1}^{\delta}

where ``L`` is the lag operator, ``d`` is the fractional differencing
parameter, and ``gamma`` controls asymmetry. The model is estimated
using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation,

.. math::

    \sigma_t^{\delta} = (1-\beta)^{-1} \omega
    + \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \lambda_i
    (|\epsilon_{t-i}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t-i})^{\delta}

The weights :math:`\lambda_i` are identical to those used in FIGARCH.

entries.name: arch.univariate.FIGARCH
entries.summary: FIGARCH model.
keywords:
FIGARCH model.

Parameters
----------
p : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation.
q : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with the innovations, abs(e) ** power.  Default is 2.0,
    which produces FIGARCH and related models. Using 1.0 produces
    FIAVARCH and related models.  Other powers can be specified, although
    these should be strictly positive, and usually larger than 0.25.
truncation : int, optional
    Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation.
    Default is 1000. Must be positive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``q`` or ``truncation`` is not an integer, or ``power`` is not a
    real number.
ValueError
    If ``p`` or ``q`` is not 0 or 1, ``truncation`` is smaller than 1, or
    ``power`` is not finite and strictly positive.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    h_t = \omega + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L)  (1-L)^d] \epsilon_t^2 + \beta h_{t-1}

where ``L`` is the lag operator and ``d`` is the fractional differencing
parameter. The model is estimated using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`)
representation,

.. math::

    h_t = (1-\beta)^{-1}  \omega + \sum_{i=1}^\infty \lambda_i \epsilon_{t-i}^2

The weights are constructed using

.. math::

    \delta_1 = d \\
    \lambda_1 = d - \beta + \phi

and the recursive equations

.. math::

    \delta_j = \frac{j - 1 - d}{j}  \delta_{j-1} \\
    \lambda_j = \beta \lambda_{j-1} + \delta_j - \phi \delta_{j-1}.

When `power` is not 2, the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation is still used
where :math:`\epsilon_t^2` is replaced by :math:`|\epsilon_t|^p` and
``p`` is the power.

entries.name: arch.univariate.GARCH
entries.summary: GARCH and related model estimation.
keywords:
GARCH and related model estimation.

The following models can be specified using GARCH:
    * ARCH(p)
    * GARCH(p,q)
    * GJR-GARCH(p,o,q)
    * AVARCH(p)
    * AVGARCH(p,q)
    * TARCH(p,o,q)
    * Models with arbitrary, pre-specified powers

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
o : int, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be
    non-negative.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with the innovations, abs(e) ** power.  Default is 2.0, which
    produces ARCH and related models. Using 1.0 produces AVARCH and related
    models.  Other powers can be specified, although these should be strictly
    positive, and usually larger than 0.25.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer, or ``power`` is not a real
    number.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, ``p`` and ``o`` are both 0, or
    ``power`` is not finite and strictly positive.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{\lambda}=\omega
    + \sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\left|\epsilon_{t-i}\right|^{\lambda}
    +\sum_{j=1}^{o}\gamma_{j}\left|\epsilon_{t-j}\right|^{\lambda}
    I\left[\epsilon_{t-j}<0\right]+\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\sigma_{t-k}^{\lambda}

where :math:`\lambda` is the ``power``.

entries.name: arch.univariate.HARCH
entries.summary: Heterogeneous ARCH process.
keywords:
Heterogeneous ARCH process.

Parameters
----------
lags : int or array_like, optional
    List of lags to include in the model, or if scalar, includes all lags up to
    the value. The lags must be positive integers, and the list cannot be empty.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` is not an integer or an array of integers.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is smaller than 1, is empty, is not 1-d, or contains a lag
    smaller than 1.

Notes
-----
In a Heterogeneous ARCH process, variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega + \sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_{l_{i}}
    \left(l_{i}^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{l_{i}}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)

In the common case where ``lags=[1,5,22]``, the model is

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+\alpha_{1}\epsilon_{t-1}^{2}
    +\alpha_{5} \left(\frac{1}{5}\sum_{j=1}^{5}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)
    +\alpha_{22} \left(\frac{1}{22}\sum_{j=1}^{22}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)

A HARCH process is a special case of an ARCH process where parameters in the
more general ARCH process have been restricted.

entries.name: arch.univariate.HARX
entries.summary: Heterogeneous Autoregression (HAR) model with optional exogenous regressors.
keywords:
Heterogeneous Autoregression (HAR) model with optional exogenous regressors.

Provides model estimation and simulation.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable.
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Array with nobs rows and k columns containing exogenous regressors.  Must
    contain only finite values.
lags : int or array_like, optional
    Description of lag structure of the HAR.

    * Scalar included all lags between 1 and the value.
    * A 1-d n-element array includes the HAR lags 1:lags[0]+1,
      1:lags[1]+1, ... 1:lags[n]+1.
    * A 2-d (2,n)-element array that includes the HAR lags of the form
      lags[0,j]:lags[1,j]+1 for all columns of lags.

    The lags must be integers (2.5, 5.0 and True are not accepted). A scalar
    must be at least 0, and the values of an array at least 1.

constant : bool, optional
    Flag whether the model should include a constant.
use_rotated : bool, optional
    Flag indicating to use the alternative rotated form of the HAR where
    HAR lags do not overlap.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.  Must be a non-negative
    integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant``, ``use_rotated`` or ``rescale`` is not
    a bool (``rescale`` can also be None), if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is
    not an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`, or if ``x`` cannot be
    converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is negative, empty or in an unsupported format, if the largest lag
    is not smaller than the number of observations, if ``hold_back`` is negative,
    or if ``x`` contains NaN or inf or does not have a row for each observation of
    ``y``.

Notes
-----
The HAR-X model is described by

.. math::

    y_t = \mu + \sum_{i=1}^p \phi_{L_{i}} \bar{y}_{t-L_{i,0}:L_{i,1}}
    + \gamma' x_t + \epsilon_t

where :math:`\bar{y}_{t-L_{i,0}:L_{i,1}}` is the average value of
:math:`y_t` between :math:`t-L_{i,0}` and :math:`t - L_{i,1}`.

entries.name: arch.univariate.MAMean
entries.summary: Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant.
keywords:
Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant.

Provides model estimation, simulation and forecasting.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable.
lags : int, optional
    The order of the moving average, q. Must be at least 1.
constant : bool, optional
    Flag whether the model should include a constant.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Must be a non-negative integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.

Attributes
----------
lags : int
    The order of the moving average
constant : bool
    Whether the model includes a constant

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool
    (``rescale`` can also be None), or if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not
    an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is smaller than 1 or ``hold_back`` is negative.

Notes
-----
The MA(q) model is

.. math::

   y_t = \mu + \epsilon_t + \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} + \ldots +
         \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q}

where the innovations :math:`\epsilon_t=\sigma_t e_t` have the conditional
variance :math:`\sigma^2_t` of the volatility process and :math:`e_t` has
the distribution of the model. The parameters are ordered
:math:`[\mu, \theta_1, \ldots, \theta_q]`, and :math:`\mu` is not included
when ``constant`` is False.

The innovations are not observed. They are computed recursively using

.. math::

   \epsilon_t = y_t - \mu - \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} - \ldots -
                \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q}

where the innovations before the first observation in the estimation sample
are 0. This is the conditional likelihood, and its effect vanishes when the
process is invertible, that is when all roots of
:math:`1+\theta_1 z+\ldots+\theta_q z^q` are outside of the unit circle.
Starting values are invertible. Invertibility is imposed when q is 1 or 2
(by bounds and linear constraints, respectively), but is not imposed for
larger q since the restrictions are nonlinear. The sample used to estimate
the parameters is also the sample used to compute the innovations, and so
observations excluded using ``hold_back`` or when fitting are not used.

The mean forecast of :math:`y_{T+h}` is
:math:`\mu + \sum_{j=h}^{q}\theta_j\epsilon_{T+h-j}`, which uses the last
:math:`q-h+1` innovations if :math:`h \leq q`, and is :math:`\mu` after
that. The forecast variance is
:math:`\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\psi_j^2\sigma^2_{T+h-j}` with :math:`\psi_0=1`,
:math:`\psi_j=\theta_j` for :math:`j\leq q` and 0 otherwise.

Exogenous regressors are not supported.

entries.name: arch.univariate.MIDASHyperbolic
entries.summary: MIDAS Hyperbolic ARCH process.
keywords:
MIDAS Hyperbolic ARCH process.

Parameters
----------
m : int, optional
    Length of maximum lag to include in the model. Must be positive.
asym : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to include an asymmetric term.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``m`` is not an integer or ``asym`` is not a bool.
ValueError
    If ``m`` is smaller than 1.

Notes
-----
In a MIDAS Hyperbolic process, the variance evolves according to

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\alpha+\gamma I\left[\epsilon_{t-j}<0\right]\right)
    \phi_{i}(\theta)\epsilon_{t-i}^{2}

where

.. math::

    \phi_{i}(\theta) \propto \Gamma(i+\theta)/(\Gamma(i+1)\Gamma(\theta))

where :math:`\Gamma` is the gamma function. :math:`\{\phi_i(\theta)\}` is
normalized so that :math:`\sum \phi_i(\theta)=1`. See [1]_ and [2]_ for
further details.

References
----------
.. [1] Foroni, Claudia, and Massimiliano Marcellino. "A survey of
   Econometric Methods for Mixed-Frequency Data". Norges Bank. (2013).
.. [2] Sheppard, Kevin. "Direct volatility modeling". Manuscript. (2018).

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``p`` is smaller than 1, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, or ``o`` is larger
    than ``p``.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega
    +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}
    \left(\epsilon_{t-i}-\theta_{i}I_{[o\geq i]}\sigma_{t-i}\right)^{2}
    +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}\sigma_{t-j}^{2}

which is :math:`\sigma_{t-i}^2 (e_{t-i}-\theta_{i})^2` in terms of the
standardized shock :math:`e_{t}=\epsilon_{t}/\sigma_{t}`. The parameters are
named ``omega``, ``alpha[i]``, ``theta[i]`` and ``beta[j]``.

The shift :math:`\theta` is the position of the minimum of the news impact curve
in units of the lagged volatility. The sign convention is that of the rugarch
package and of most textbooks: a positive :math:`\theta` is the leverage effect,
since a negative shock then raises the variance more than a positive shock of
the same size. Engle and Ng [1]_ write the shift as
:math:`(\epsilon_{t-1}+\gamma\sigma_{t-1})^2` and expect :math:`\gamma<0`, so
that :math:`\theta=-\gamma`.

The name NGARCH is also used for the nonlinear ARCH model of Higgins and
Bera [2]_, which is a different model and is not available here.

The expected value of :math:`(e_{t}-\theta)^2` is :math:`1+\theta^2` for any
standardized distribution, since :math:`e_t` has mean 0 and variance 1. The
process is covariance stationary if the persistence

.. math::

    \phi=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\left(1+\theta_{i}^{2}\right)
    +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}

is smaller than 1, and then the unconditional variance of :math:`\epsilon_t` is
:math:`\omega/(1-\phi)`. Analytic forecasts are exact at every horizon. When
:math:`p=q=1`, they satisfy :math:`f_h=\omega+\phi f_{h-1}`.

Estimation uses the linear constraints :math:`\omega,\alpha_i,\beta_j\geq 0` and
:math:`\sum\alpha_i+\sum\beta_j<1`, as for :class:`~arch.univariate.APARCH`,
and bounds of -5 and 5 for :math:`\theta`. The stationarity condition
:math:`\phi<1` is not imposed during estimation, since it is not linear in the
parameters, and a model with :math:`\theta\neq 0` can be estimated with a
persistence of 1 or more. ``fit`` then issues a ``ValueWarning``.

With ``o=0`` there is no shift and the process is a GARCH process, so
:class:`~arch.univariate.GARCH` should be used instead. A ``ValueWarning`` is
issued in this case.

Before the start of the sample, the variance and the squared residual are both
replaced by the backcast of the variance, so that each shock term is
:math:`\alpha_i(1+\theta_i^2)` times the backcast.

References
----------
.. [1] Engle, R. F., & Ng, V. K. (1993). Measuring and testing the impact of
   news on volatility. *The Journal of Finance*, 48(5), 1749-1778.
.. [2] Higgins, M. L., & Bera, A. K. (1992). A class of nonlinear ARCH models.
   *International Economic Review*, 33(1), 137-158.

Parameters

tau0 : int or float, optional
    Length of long cycle. Default is 1560. Must be finite and larger than
    ``tau1``.
tau1 : int or float, optional
    Length of short cycle. Default is 4. Must be finite and positive.
kmax : int, optional
    Number of components. Default is 14. Must be positive, and
    ``tau1 * rho ** (kmax - 1)`` cannot be larger than ``tau0``.
rho : float, optional

    larger than 1.

    integer.
ValueError

    ``tau0`` is not larger than ``tau1``, ``kmax`` is smaller than 1, ``rho`` is
    not larger than 1, or ``tau1 * rho ** (kmax - 1)`` is larger than ``tau0``.

Notes
-----
The variance dynamics of the model are given as a weighted average of kmax EWMA
variance processes where the smoothing parameters and weights are determined by
tau0, tau1 and rho.

This model has no parameters since the smoothing parameter is fixed.

entries.name: arch.univariate.arch_model
entries.summary: Initialize common ARCH model specifications.
keywords:
Initialize common ARCH model specifications.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like, Series or None
    The dependent variable.
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Exogenous regressors.  Ignored if model does not permit exogenous
    regressors.
mean : str, optional
    Name of the mean model.  Currently supported options are: 'constant'
    (default), 'zero', 'ls', 'ar', 'arx', 'har' and 'harx'.  Not case
    sensitive.
lags : int or list of int, optional
    Either a scalar integer value indicating lag length or a list of
    integers specifying lag locations.
vol : str, optional
    Name of the volatility model.  Currently supported options are:
    'garch' (default), 'arch', 'egarch', 'figarch', 'fiaparch', 'aparch',
    'harch' and 'ngarch'.  Not case sensitive.
p : int or list of int, optional
    Lag order of the symmetric innovation.  A list of lags can only be used
    with the 'harch' volatility model.  Must be at least 0, and integers
    only (2.0 and True are not accepted).
o : int, optional
    Lag order of the asymmetric innovation.  Must be at least 0.
q : int, optional
    Lag order of lagged volatility or equivalent.  Must be at least 0.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with GARCH and related models.  Must be finite and positive.
dist : str, optional
    Name of the error distribution.  Not case sensitive.  Currently
    supported options are:

        * Normal: 'normal', 'gaussian' (default)
        * Student's t: 't', 'studentst'
        * Skewed Student's t: 'skewstudent', 'skewt'
        * Generalized Error Distribution: 'ged', 'generalized error'

hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale
    of the data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating
    model parameters. If False, the model is estimated on the data without
    transformation.  If True, then y is rescaled and the new scale is
    reported in the estimation results.

Returns
-------
model : ARCHModel
    Configured ARCH model.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``mean``, ``vol`` or ``dist`` is not a string, ``lags``, ``p``, ``o``,
    ``q`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), ``rescale`` is not a bool or None, ``power`` is not
    a real number, or ``x`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``mean``, ``vol`` or ``dist`` is not one of the options, ``lags``, ``p``,
    ``o``, ``q`` or ``hold_back`` is negative, ``o`` is 0 when
    ``vol='ngarch'``, ``power`` is not finite and positive, or ``x`` contains
    NaN or inf or does not have a row for each observation of ``y``.

Notes
-----
Input that are not relevant for a particular specification, such as `lags`
when `mean='zero'`, are silently ignored, and so are not checked.

The default ``o=0`` has no asymmetric term in any volatility model. With
``vol='ngarch'``, ``o`` is the number of shifted innovations, and must not exceed
``p``. Use ``o=1`` for the NGARCH(1,1) of Engle and Ng. An NGARCH model without
a shift is a GARCH model, and so ``vol='ngarch'`` with the default ``o=0``
raises a ``ValueError``.
