entries.name: arch.univariate.backtest.christoffersen_conditional_coverage
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR.
keywords:
Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_2` under the null that exceptions are independent and have
    probability ``p``, with its p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is
    not a real number.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, there
    are fewer than 2 observations, or ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5].

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.
christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions.

Notes
-----
The statistic of Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is the sum of the Kupiec statistic,
computed with all the observations, and the independence statistic,
:math:`LR_{cc}=LR_{uc}+LR_{ind}`. See `kupiec_pof` and
`christoffersen_independence` for the statistics and for the handling of
series with no exceptions or with only exceptions.

References
----------
.. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts.
   International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.backtest.christoffersen_independence
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords:
Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that exceptions are independent, with its
    p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or there
    are fewer than 2 observations.

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.
christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence.

Notes
-----
The null is that the probability of an exception does not depend on whether
the previous day was an exception, against a first-order Markov chain. With
:math:`n_{ij}` the number of days in state :math:`j` that follow a day in
state :math:`i` (1 is an exception), :math:`\hat{\pi}_{i}=n_{i1}/(n_{i0}+n_{i1})`
and :math:`\hat{\pi}=(n_{01}+n_{11})/\sum n_{ij}`, the statistic of
Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is

.. math::

    LR_{ind} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-\hat{\pi})^{n_{00}+n_{10}}
               \hat{\pi}^{n_{01}+n_{11}}}
               {(1-\hat{\pi}_0)^{n_{00}}\hat{\pi}_0^{n_{01}}
               (1-\hat{\pi}_1)^{n_{10}}\hat{\pi}_1^{n_{11}}}\right].

The first observation is conditioned on, so the :math:`T-1` transitions are
used. A term :math:`0\ln 0` is 0. If no day follows a state, for example when
there is no exception before the last day, :math:`\hat{\pi}_i` is not defined
and does not enter the statistic. The statistic is 0 for a series with no
exceptions or only exceptions. A probability that is 0, because no exception
follows an exception (:math:`n_{11}=0`), is evaluated at the limit.

References
----------
.. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts.
   International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.backtest.kupiec_pof
entries.summary: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR.
keywords:
Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that the probability of an exception is
    ``p``, with its p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is
    not a real number.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or ``p``
    is not in (0, 0.5].

See Also
--------
christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions.
christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence.
traffic_light : The Basel zone of the number of exceptions.

Notes
-----
With :math:`x` exceptions in :math:`T` observations and
:math:`\hat{\pi}=x/T`, the statistic of Kupiec (1995) [1]_ is

.. math::

    LR_{uc} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-p)^{T-x}p^x}
              {(1-\hat{\pi})^{T-x}\hat{\pi}^x}\right].

The test is two-sided, so too few exceptions reject as well as too many.
The terms :math:`0\ln 0` of a series with no exception, or only exceptions,
are 0, which is the limit of the likelihood, so that the statistic is
:math:`-2T\ln(1-p)` and :math:`-2T\ln p`.

References
----------
.. [1] Kupiec, P. H. (1995). Techniques for verifying the accuracy of risk
   measurement models. The Journal of Derivatives, 3(2), 73-84.

entries.name: arch.univariate.backtest.traffic_light
entries.summary: Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords:
Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least ``window``
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.01, the 99% VaR of the Basel
    framework.
window : int, optional
    The number of the most recent observations that are counted. It must be
    positive and no larger than the number of observations. The default is
    250, about one year of daily data.

Returns
-------
TrafficLightResult
    The zone, the number of exceptions in the window, the cumulative binomial
    probability of that number of exceptions or fewer, the probability of that
    number or more (the type 1 error), the number of observations in the window
    and ``p``.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, ``p`` is not a
    real number or ``window`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, ``p`` is
    not in (0, 0.5], ``window`` is not positive, or there are fewer than
    ``window`` observations.

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.

Notes
-----
The framework of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996) [1]_ counts the
exceptions in the last 250 days. If the probability of an exception is ``p``,
the number of exceptions has a binomial distribution, and the cumulative
probability :math:`P(X\leq x)` of the observed number :math:`x` sets the zone.
The zone is green if the probability is below 95%, yellow if it is at least 95%
and below 99.99%, and red if it is at least 99.99%, since the framework says
that the yellow and the red zone begin where the probability equals or exceeds
95% and 99.99%. For 250 observations and ``p=0.01``, green is 0 to 4
exceptions, yellow is 5 to 9 and red is 10 or more, which are the boundaries of
Table 2 of the framework. The framework deduces the boundaries for other sample
sizes from the binomial distribution in the same way, as this function does.

``type1_error`` is :math:`P(X\geq x)`, the probability that an accurate model
has :math:`x` or more exceptions. The two probabilities add up to more than 1
by the probability of exactly :math:`x` exceptions.

A series with no exception is always green. Its cumulative probability is the
probability of the smallest number of exceptions, which is above 95% when
``window * p`` is small, but no exception is never a sign of understated risk.

A series with fewer than ``window`` observations raises an error rather than
being tested with the observations that there are, because the zones of the
framework are defined for a sample of the specified size. Set ``window`` to
the number of observations to test a shorter series.

References
----------
.. [1] Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996). Supervisory framework
   for the use of "backtesting" in conjunction with the internal models
   approach to market risk capital requirements.

entries.name: arch.univariate.backtest.var_exceptions
entries.summary: Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast.
keywords:
Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts, a 1-d array of finite numbers. VaR is a positive loss,
    so that a VaR of 2.5 forecasts that the return is below -2.5 with the
    probability that the VaR is designed for. If both ``returns`` and ``var``
    are Series, they are aligned on the index and the observations that are
    in both are used, in the order of ``returns``. Otherwise, they must have
    the same length and are matched by position.

Returns
-------
{ndarray, Series}
    A bool array that is True where the return is an exception, that is
    where the loss exceeds the VaR, ``-returns > var``. It is a Series named
    ``"exception"`` if ``returns`` or ``var`` is a pandas object, with the
    index of the observations that are used: the index of ``returns`` if it
    is a pandas object, and otherwise the index of ``var``.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not a 1-d array of finite numbers (NaN and
    inf raise), has no observations, has an index with duplicates that
    differs from the index of the other Series, or does not have the same
    length as the other input.

Notes
-----
The sign convention is the same for all the functions of this module. VaR is
reported as a positive loss, so that a 99% VaR of 2.5 is the loss that is
exceeded with probability ``p=0.01``, and an observation is an exception if
:math:`-r_t > \mathrm{VaR}_t`. A quantile of the distribution of returns,
which is negative for the lower tail, must be negated first. A loss that
equals the VaR is not an exception.

Only two Series are aligned on the index. A DataFrame, an array, or a Series
used with an array, is matched by position, so the VaR forecast for the
return in position :math:`t` must be in position :math:`t`. The forecasts
of :meth:`~arch.univariate.base.ARCHModelResult.forecast` are indexed by the
date of the forecast origin by default, so that the one-step forecast for
day :math:`t` has the label of day :math:`t-1`. Use
``forecast(..., align="target")``, or shift the VaR forward by one
observation, so that each VaR has the label of the return that it is a
forecast of.

entries.name: arch.univariate.base.ARCHModel
entries.summary: Abstract base class for mean models in ARCH processes.
keywords:
Abstract base class for mean models in ARCH processes.

Specifies the conditional mean process.

All public methods that raise NotImplementedError should be overridden by
any subclass.  Private methods that raise NotImplementedError are optional
to override but recommended where applicable.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    The dependent variable.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model.  If not specified, a constant
    variance is used.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Distribution of the standardized residuals.  If not specified, a standard
    normal is used.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.  Must not be negative.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``volatility`` is not a VolatilityProcess, ``distribution`` is not a
    Distribution, ``hold_back`` is not an integer or ``rescale`` is not a bool.
ValueError
    If ``hold_back`` is negative or ``y`` contains NaN or inf.

entries.name: arch.univariate.christoffersen_conditional_coverage
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR.
keywords:
Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_2` under the null that exceptions are independent and have
    probability ``p``, with its p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is
    not a real number.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, there
    are fewer than 2 observations, or ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5].

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.
christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions.

Notes
-----
The statistic of Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is the sum of the Kupiec statistic,
computed with all the observations, and the independence statistic,
:math:`LR_{cc}=LR_{uc}+LR_{ind}`. See `kupiec_pof` and
`christoffersen_independence` for the statistics and for the handling of
series with no exceptions or with only exceptions.

References
----------
.. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts.
   International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.christoffersen_independence
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords:
Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that exceptions are independent, with its
    p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or there
    are fewer than 2 observations.

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.
christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence.

Notes
-----
The null is that the probability of an exception does not depend on whether
the previous day was an exception, against a first-order Markov chain. With
:math:`n_{ij}` the number of days in state :math:`j` that follow a day in
state :math:`i` (1 is an exception), :math:`\hat{\pi}_{i}=n_{i1}/(n_{i0}+n_{i1})`
and :math:`\hat{\pi}=(n_{01}+n_{11})/\sum n_{ij}`, the statistic of
Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is

.. math::

    LR_{ind} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-\hat{\pi})^{n_{00}+n_{10}}
               \hat{\pi}^{n_{01}+n_{11}}}
               {(1-\hat{\pi}_0)^{n_{00}}\hat{\pi}_0^{n_{01}}
               (1-\hat{\pi}_1)^{n_{10}}\hat{\pi}_1^{n_{11}}}\right].

The first observation is conditioned on, so the :math:`T-1` transitions are
used. A term :math:`0\ln 0` is 0. If no day follows a state, for example when
there is no exception before the last day, :math:`\hat{\pi}_i` is not defined
and does not enter the statistic. The statistic is 0 for a series with no
exceptions or only exceptions. A probability that is 0, because no exception
follows an exception (:math:`n_{11}=0`), is evaluated at the limit.

References
----------
.. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts.
   International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.diagnostics.hill_estimator
entries.summary: Hill tail-index estimator of standardized residuals.
keywords:
Hill tail-index estimator of standardized residuals.

Parameters
----------
std_resid : array_like
    Standardized residuals. The estimator is computed from the largest
    absolute standardized residuals after removing non-finite observations,
    since the residuals of a fitted model are NaN outside the estimation
    sample.
k : int, optional
    Number of upper order statistics to use. If not provided, uses
    ``int(sqrt(n))`` where ``n`` is the number of finite residuals. Must be at
    least 1 and less than the number of non-zero finite residuals.

Returns
-------
float
    Inverse Hill estimate of the tail index.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``std_resid`` cannot be converted to numbers or ``k`` is not an
    integer.
ValueError
    If ``std_resid`` is not 1-d, has fewer than two non-zero finite
    observations, or ``k`` is outside the allowed range.

Notes
-----
The estimator is

.. math::

    \hat{\nu} = \left(k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k
    \log X_{n-i+1:n} - \log X_{n-k:n}\right)^{-1}

where ``X`` contains the positive absolute standardized residuals.

entries.name: arch.univariate.diagnostics.var_ratio
entries.summary: Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR.
keywords:
Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR.

Parameters
----------
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the open interval (0, 0.5). It is 0.05 for a 95%
    VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.001, a 99.9% VaR.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Standardized distribution used to compute the model VaR. If not
    provided, uses the standard normal distribution.
parameters : array_like, optional
    Distribution parameters. Must have one finite element for each parameter
    of ``distribution``. Use ``None`` for parameterless distributions.

Returns
-------
float
    Ratio of the Gaussian left-tail VaR to the VaR implied by the supplied
    model distribution.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p`` is not a real number, ``distribution`` is not a Distribution or
    ``parameters`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5), ``parameters`` does not have one finite
    element for each parameter of the distribution, or the model distribution
    does not produce a positive finite VaR.

Notes
-----
VaR is named by its confidence level, and ``p`` is the probability of an
exception, as in the VaR backtests such as :func:`~arch.univariate.kupiec_pof`.
The ratio is :math:`\Phi^{-1}(p)/F^{-1}(p)` where :math:`F` is the
standardized distribution.

entries.name: arch.univariate.kupiec_pof
entries.summary: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR.
keywords:
Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR.

Returns
-------
arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic
    The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically
    :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that the probability of an exception is
    ``p``, with its p-value.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is
    not a real number.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or ``p``
    is not in (0, 0.5].

See Also
--------
christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions.
christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence.
traffic_light : The Basel zone of the number of exceptions.

Notes
-----
With :math:`x` exceptions in :math:`T` observations and
:math:`\hat{\pi}=x/T`, the statistic of Kupiec (1995) [1]_ is

.. math::

    LR_{uc} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-p)^{T-x}p^x}
              {(1-\hat{\pi})^{T-x}\hat{\pi}^x}\right].

The test is two-sided, so too few exceptions reject as well as too many.
The terms :math:`0\ln 0` of a series with no exception, or only exceptions,
are 0, which is the limit of the likelihood, so that the statistic is
:math:`-2T\ln(1-p)` and :math:`-2T\ln p`.

References
----------
.. [1] Kupiec, P. H. (1995). Techniques for verifying the accuracy of risk
   measurement models. The Journal of Derivatives, 3(2), 73-84.

entries.name: arch.univariate.mean.ARCHInMean
entries.summary: (G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation.
keywords:
(G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable.
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Array with nobs rows and k columns containing exogenous regressors.  Must
    contain only finite values.
lags : int or array_like, optional
    Description of lag structure of the AR.  Scalar included all lags
    between 1 and the value.  A 1-d array includes the AR lags lags[0],
    lags[1], ...  The lags must be integers (2.5, 5.0 and True are not
    accepted). A scalar must be at least 0, and the values of an array at
    least 1.
constant : bool, optional
    Flag whether the model should include a constant.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.  Must be a non-negative
    integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model. ``volatility.updateable`` must
    return ``True``.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.
form : {"log", "vol", "var"}, int or float, optional
    The form of the conditional variance that appears in the mean equation. The
    string names use the log of the conditional variance ("log"), the square-root
    of the conditional variance ("vol") or the conditional variance. When
    specified using a float, interpreted as :math:`\sigma_t^{form}` so that
    1 is equivalent to "vol" and 2 is equivalent to "var". When using a number,
    must be finite and different from 0.  The strings are not case sensitive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool
    (``rescale`` can also be None), if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not
    an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`, or if ``x`` cannot be
    converted to numbers, or if ``form`` is not a string or a number.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is negative, empty or in an unsupported format, if the largest lag
    is not smaller than the number of observations, if ``hold_back`` is negative,
    if ``form`` is a string other than "log", "vol" or "var" or is not finite or
    is 0, or if ``x`` contains NaN or inf or does not have a row for each
    observation of ``y``.

Notes
-----
The (G)arch-in-mean model with exogenous regressors (-X)  is described by

.. math::

    y_t = \mu + \kappa f(\sigma^2_t)+ \sum_{i=1}^p \phi_{L_{i}} y_{t-L_{i}}
          + \gamma' x_t +  \epsilon_t

where :math:`f(\cdot)` is the function specified by ``form``.

      lags[0,j]:lags[1,j]+1 for all columns of lags.

    HAR lags do not overlap.

    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.  Must be a non-negative
    integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant``, ``use_rotated`` or ``rescale`` is not
    a bool (``rescale`` can also be None), if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is
    not an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`, or if ``x`` cannot be
    converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is negative, empty or in an unsupported format, if the largest lag
    is not smaller than the number of observations, if ``hold_back`` is negative,
    or if ``x`` contains NaN or inf or does not have a row for each observation of

    y_t = \mu + \sum_{i=1}^p \phi_{L_{i}} \bar{y}_{t-L_{i,0}:L_{i,1}}

entries.name: arch.univariate.mean.MAMean
entries.summary: Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant.
keywords:
Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant.

Provides model estimation, simulation and forecasting.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like or Series, optional
    Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable.
lags : int, optional
    The order of the moving average, q. Must be at least 1.
constant : bool, optional
    Flag whether the model should include a constant.
hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Must be a non-negative integer.
volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional
    Volatility process to use in the model.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Error distribution to use in the model.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the
    data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters.
    If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation.  If True,
    then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results.
    If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is
    likely to produce convergence issues.

Attributes
----------
lags : int
    The order of the moving average
constant : bool
    Whether the model includes a constant

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool
    (``rescale`` can also be None), or if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not
    an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or
    :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is smaller than 1 or ``hold_back`` is negative.

Notes
-----
The MA(q) model is

.. math::

   y_t = \mu + \epsilon_t + \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} + \ldots +
         \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q}

where the innovations :math:`\epsilon_t=\sigma_t e_t` have the conditional
variance :math:`\sigma^2_t` of the volatility process and :math:`e_t` has
the distribution of the model. The parameters are ordered
:math:`[\mu, \theta_1, \ldots, \theta_q]`, and :math:`\mu` is not included
when ``constant`` is False.

The innovations are not observed. They are computed recursively using

.. math::

   \epsilon_t = y_t - \mu - \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} - \ldots -
                \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q}

where the innovations before the first observation in the estimation sample
are 0. This is the conditional likelihood, and its effect vanishes when the
process is invertible, that is when all roots of
:math:`1+\theta_1 z+\ldots+\theta_q z^q` are outside of the unit circle.
Starting values are invertible. Invertibility is imposed when q is 1 or 2
(by bounds and linear constraints, respectively), but is not imposed for
larger q since the restrictions are nonlinear. The sample used to estimate
the parameters is also the sample used to compute the innovations, and so
observations excluded using ``hold_back`` or when fitting are not used.

The mean forecast of :math:`y_{T+h}` is
:math:`\mu + \sum_{j=h}^{q}\theta_j\epsilon_{T+h-j}`, which uses the last
:math:`q-h+1` innovations if :math:`h \leq q`, and is :math:`\mu` after
that. The forecast variance is
:math:`\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\psi_j^2\sigma^2_{T+h-j}` with :math:`\psi_0=1`,
:math:`\psi_j=\theta_j` for :math:`j\leq q` and 0 otherwise.

Exogenous regressors are not supported.

entries.name: arch.univariate.mean.arch_model
entries.summary: Initialize common ARCH model specifications.
keywords:
Initialize common ARCH model specifications.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like, Series or None
    The dependent variable.
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Exogenous regressors.  Ignored if model does not permit exogenous
    regressors.
mean : str, optional
    Name of the mean model.  Currently supported options are: 'constant'
    (default), 'zero', 'ls', 'ar', 'arx', 'har' and 'harx'.  Not case
    sensitive.
lags : int or list of int, optional
    Either a scalar integer value indicating lag length or a list of
    integers specifying lag locations.
vol : str, optional
    Name of the volatility model.  Currently supported options are:
    'garch' (default), 'arch', 'egarch', 'figarch', 'fiaparch', 'aparch',
    'harch' and 'ngarch'.  Not case sensitive.
p : int or list of int, optional
    Lag order of the symmetric innovation.  A list of lags can only be used
    with the 'harch' volatility model.  Must be at least 0, and integers
    only (2.0 and True are not accepted).
o : int, optional
    Lag order of the asymmetric innovation.  Must be at least 0.
q : int, optional
    Lag order of lagged volatility or equivalent.  Must be at least 0.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with GARCH and related models.  Must be finite and positive.
dist : str, optional
    Name of the error distribution.  Not case sensitive.  Currently
    supported options are:

        * Normal: 'normal', 'gaussian' (default)
        * Student's t: 't', 'studentst'
        * Skewed Student's t: 'skewstudent', 'skewt'
        * Generalized Error Distribution: 'ged', 'generalized error'

hold_back : int, optional
    Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when
    estimating model parameters.  Used when comparing models with different
    lag lengths to estimate on the common sample.
rescale : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale
    of the data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating
    model parameters. If False, the model is estimated on the data without
    transformation.  If True, then y is rescaled and the new scale is
    reported in the estimation results.

Returns
-------
model : ARCHModel
    Configured ARCH model.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``mean``, ``vol`` or ``dist`` is not a string, ``lags``, ``p``, ``o``,
    ``q`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a
    bool are not accepted), ``rescale`` is not a bool or None, ``power`` is not
    a real number, or ``x`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``mean``, ``vol`` or ``dist`` is not one of the options, ``lags``, ``p``,
    ``o``, ``q`` or ``hold_back`` is negative, ``o`` is 0 when
    ``vol='ngarch'``, ``power`` is not finite and positive, or ``x`` contains
    NaN or inf or does not have a row for each observation of ``y``.

Notes
-----
Input that are not relevant for a particular specification, such as `lags`
when `mean='zero'`, are silently ignored, and so are not checked.

The default ``o=0`` has no asymmetric term in any volatility model. With
``vol='ngarch'``, ``o`` is the number of shifted innovations, and must not exceed
``p``. Use ``o=1`` for the NGARCH(1,1) of Engle and Ng. An NGARCH model without
a shift is a GARCH model, and so ``vol='ngarch'`` with the default ``o=0``
raises a ``ValueError``.

entries.name: arch.univariate.traffic_light
entries.summary: Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords:
Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least ``window``
    observations.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See
    `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are
    aligned.
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR
    and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.01, the 99% VaR of the Basel
    framework.
window : int, optional
    The number of the most recent observations that are counted. It must be
    positive and no larger than the number of observations. The default is
    250, about one year of daily data.

Returns
-------
TrafficLightResult
    The zone, the number of exceptions in the window, the cumulative binomial
    probability of that number of exceptions or fewer, the probability of that
    number or more (the type 1 error), the number of observations in the window
    and ``p``.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, ``p`` is not a
    real number or ``window`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, ``p`` is
    not in (0, 0.5], ``window`` is not positive, or there are fewer than
    ``window`` observations.

See Also
--------
kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions.

Notes
-----
The framework of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996) [1]_ counts the
exceptions in the last 250 days. If the probability of an exception is ``p``,
the number of exceptions has a binomial distribution, and the cumulative
probability :math:`P(X\leq x)` of the observed number :math:`x` sets the zone.
The zone is green if the probability is below 95%, yellow if it is at least 95%
and below 99.99%, and red if it is at least 99.99%, since the framework says
that the yellow and the red zone begin where the probability equals or exceeds
95% and 99.99%. For 250 observations and ``p=0.01``, green is 0 to 4
exceptions, yellow is 5 to 9 and red is 10 or more, which are the boundaries of
Table 2 of the framework. The framework deduces the boundaries for other sample
sizes from the binomial distribution in the same way, as this function does.

``type1_error`` is :math:`P(X\geq x)`, the probability that an accurate model
has :math:`x` or more exceptions. The two probabilities add up to more than 1
by the probability of exactly :math:`x` exceptions.

A series with no exception is always green. Its cumulative probability is the
probability of the smallest number of exceptions, which is above 95% when
``window * p`` is small, but no exception is never a sign of understated risk.

A series with fewer than ``window`` observations raises an error rather than
being tested with the observations that there are, because the zones of the
framework are defined for a sample of the specified size. Set ``window`` to
the number of observations to test a shorter series.

References
----------
.. [1] Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996). Supervisory framework
   for the use of "backtesting" in conjunction with the internal models
   approach to market risk capital requirements.

entries.name: arch.univariate.var_exceptions
entries.summary: Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast.
keywords:
Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast.

Parameters
----------
returns : array_like
    Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers.
var : array_like
    VaR forecasts, a 1-d array of finite numbers. VaR is a positive loss,
    so that a VaR of 2.5 forecasts that the return is below -2.5 with the
    probability that the VaR is designed for. If both ``returns`` and ``var``
    are Series, they are aligned on the index and the observations that are
    in both are used, in the order of ``returns``. Otherwise, they must have
    the same length and are matched by position.

Returns
-------
{ndarray, Series}
    A bool array that is True where the return is an exception, that is
    where the loss exceeds the VaR, ``-returns > var``. It is a Series named
    ``"exception"`` if ``returns`` or ``var`` is a pandas object, with the
    index of the observations that are used: the index of ``returns`` if it
    is a pandas object, and otherwise the index of ``var``.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not a 1-d array of finite numbers (NaN and
    inf raise), has no observations, has an index with duplicates that
    differs from the index of the other Series, or does not have the same
    length as the other input.

Notes
-----
The sign convention is the same for all the functions of this module. VaR is
reported as a positive loss, so that a 99% VaR of 2.5 is the loss that is
exceeded with probability ``p=0.01``, and an observation is an exception if
:math:`-r_t > \mathrm{VaR}_t`. A quantile of the distribution of returns,
which is negative for the lower tail, must be negated first. A loss that
equals the VaR is not an exception.

Only two Series are aligned on the index. A DataFrame, an array, or a Series
used with an array, is matched by position, so the VaR forecast for the
return in position :math:`t` must be in position :math:`t`. The forecasts
of :meth:`~arch.univariate.base.ARCHModelResult.forecast` are indexed by the
date of the forecast origin by default, so that the one-step forecast for
day :math:`t` has the label of day :math:`t-1`. Use
``forecast(..., align="target")``, or shift the VaR forward by one
observation, so that each VaR has the label of the return that it is a
forecast of.

entries.name: arch.univariate.var_ratio
entries.summary: Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR.
keywords:
Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR.

Parameters
----------
p : float, optional
    The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is
    the size of the tail, in the open interval (0, 0.5). It is 0.05 for a 95%
    VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.001, a 99.9% VaR.
distribution : Distribution, optional
    Standardized distribution used to compute the model VaR. If not
    provided, uses the standard normal distribution.
parameters : array_like, optional
    Distribution parameters. Must have one finite element for each parameter
    of ``distribution``. Use ``None`` for parameterless distributions.

Returns
-------
float
    Ratio of the Gaussian left-tail VaR to the VaR implied by the supplied
    model distribution.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p`` is not a real number, ``distribution`` is not a Distribution or
    ``parameters`` cannot be converted to numbers.
ValueError
    If ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5), ``parameters`` does not have one finite
    element for each parameter of the distribution, or the model distribution
    does not produce a positive finite VaR.

Notes
-----
VaR is named by its confidence level, and ``p`` is the probability of an
exception, as in the VaR backtests such as :func:`~arch.univariate.kupiec_pof`.
The ratio is :math:`\Phi^{-1}(p)/F^{-1}(p)` where :math:`F` is the
standardized distribution.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.EGARCH
entries.summary: EGARCH model estimation.
keywords:
EGARCH model estimation.

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
o : int, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be
    non-negative.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, or ``p`` and ``o`` are both 0.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \ln\sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega
    +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}
    \left(\left|e_{t-i}\right|-\sqrt{2/\pi}\right)
    +\sum_{j=1}^{o}\gamma_{j} e_{t-j}
    +\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\ln\sigma_{t-k}^{2}

where :math:`e_{t}=\epsilon_{t}/\sigma_{t}`.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.FIAPARCH
entries.summary: Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process.
keywords:
Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process.

Parameters
----------
p : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation.
o : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation.
q : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance.
delta : float, optional
    Value to use for a fixed delta in the model. If not provided,
    the value of delta is jointly estimated with other model parameters.
    User provided delta is restricted to lie in (0.05, 4.0).
truncation : int, optional
    Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation.
    Default is 1000. Must be positive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o``, ``q`` or ``truncation`` is not an integer, or ``delta`` is
    not a real number or None.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not 0 or 1, ``truncation`` is smaller than 1, or
    ``delta`` is NaN, inf or not in (0.05, 4.0).

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_t^{\delta} = \omega
    + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L)(1-L)^d]
    (|\epsilon_{t}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t})^{\delta}
    + \beta \sigma_{t-1}^{\delta}

where ``L`` is the lag operator, ``d`` is the fractional differencing
parameter, and ``gamma`` controls asymmetry. The model is estimated
using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation,

.. math::

    \sigma_t^{\delta} = (1-\beta)^{-1} \omega
    + \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \lambda_i
    (|\epsilon_{t-i}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t-i})^{\delta}

The weights :math:`\lambda_i` are identical to those used in FIGARCH.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.FIGARCH
entries.summary: FIGARCH model.
keywords:
FIGARCH model.

Parameters
----------
p : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation.
q : {0, 1}, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with the innovations, abs(e) ** power.  Default is 2.0,
    which produces FIGARCH and related models. Using 1.0 produces
    FIAVARCH and related models.  Other powers can be specified, although
    these should be strictly positive, and usually larger than 0.25.
truncation : int, optional
    Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation.
    Default is 1000. Must be positive.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``q`` or ``truncation`` is not an integer, or ``power`` is not a
    real number.
ValueError
    If ``p`` or ``q`` is not 0 or 1, ``truncation`` is smaller than 1, or
    ``power`` is not finite and strictly positive.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    h_t = \omega + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L)  (1-L)^d] \epsilon_t^2 + \beta h_{t-1}

where ``L`` is the lag operator and ``d`` is the fractional differencing
parameter. The model is estimated using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`)
representation,

.. math::

    h_t = (1-\beta)^{-1}  \omega + \sum_{i=1}^\infty \lambda_i \epsilon_{t-i}^2

The weights are constructed using

.. math::

    \delta_1 = d \\
    \lambda_1 = d - \beta + \phi

and the recursive equations

.. math::

    \delta_j = \frac{j - 1 - d}{j}  \delta_{j-1} \\
    \lambda_j = \beta \lambda_{j-1} + \delta_j - \phi \delta_{j-1}.

When `power` is not 2, the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation is still used
where :math:`\epsilon_t^2` is replaced by :math:`|\epsilon_t|^p` and
``p`` is the power.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.GARCH
entries.summary: GARCH and related model estimation.
keywords:
GARCH and related model estimation.

The following models can be specified using GARCH:
    * ARCH(p)
    * GARCH(p,q)
    * GJR-GARCH(p,o,q)
    * AVARCH(p)
    * AVGARCH(p,q)
    * TARCH(p,o,q)
    * Models with arbitrary, pre-specified powers

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
o : int, optional
    Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must be non-negative.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be
    non-negative.
power : float, optional
    Power to use with the innovations, abs(e) ** power.  Default is 2.0, which
    produces ARCH and related models. Using 1.0 produces AVARCH and related
    models.  Other powers can be specified, although these should be strictly
    positive, and usually larger than 0.25.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer, or ``power`` is not a real
    number.
ValueError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, ``p`` and ``o`` are both 0, or
    ``power`` is not finite and strictly positive.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{\lambda}=\omega
    + \sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\left|\epsilon_{t-i}\right|^{\lambda}
    +\sum_{j=1}^{o}\gamma_{j}\left|\epsilon_{t-j}\right|^{\lambda}
    I\left[\epsilon_{t-j}<0\right]+\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\sigma_{t-k}^{\lambda}

where :math:`\lambda` is the ``power``.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.HARCH
entries.summary: Heterogeneous ARCH process.
keywords:
Heterogeneous ARCH process.

Parameters
----------
lags : int or array_like, optional
    List of lags to include in the model, or if scalar, includes all lags up to
    the value. The lags must be positive integers, and the list cannot be empty.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``lags`` is not an integer or an array of integers.
ValueError
    If ``lags`` is smaller than 1, is empty, is not 1-d, or contains a lag
    smaller than 1.

Notes
-----
In a Heterogeneous ARCH process, variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega + \sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_{l_{i}}
    \left(l_{i}^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{l_{i}}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)

In the common case where ``lags=[1,5,22]``, the model is

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+\alpha_{1}\epsilon_{t-1}^{2}
    +\alpha_{5} \left(\frac{1}{5}\sum_{j=1}^{5}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)
    +\alpha_{22} \left(\frac{1}{22}\sum_{j=1}^{22}\epsilon_{t-j}^{2}\right)

A HARCH process is a special case of an ARCH process where parameters in the
more general ARCH process have been restricted.

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.MIDASHyperbolic
entries.summary: MIDAS Hyperbolic ARCH process.
keywords:
MIDAS Hyperbolic ARCH process.

Parameters
----------
m : int, optional
    Length of maximum lag to include in the model. Must be positive.
asym : bool, optional
    Flag indicating whether to include an asymmetric term.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``m`` is not an integer or ``asym`` is not a bool.
ValueError
    If ``m`` is smaller than 1.

Notes
-----
In a MIDAS Hyperbolic process, the variance evolves according to

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega+
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\alpha+\gamma I\left[\epsilon_{t-j}<0\right]\right)
    \phi_{i}(\theta)\epsilon_{t-i}^{2}

where

.. math::

    \phi_{i}(\theta) \propto \Gamma(i+\theta)/(\Gamma(i+1)\Gamma(\theta))

where :math:`\Gamma` is the gamma function. :math:`\{\phi_i(\theta)\}` is
normalized so that :math:`\sum \phi_i(\theta)=1`. See [1]_ and [2]_ for
further details.

References
----------
.. [1] Foroni, Claudia, and Massimiliano Marcellino. "A survey of
   Econometric Methods for Mixed-Frequency Data". Norges Bank. (2013).
.. [2] Sheppard, Kevin. "Direct volatility modeling". Manuscript. (2018).

entries.name: arch.univariate.volatility.NGARCH
entries.summary: Nonlinear asymmetric GARCH (NGARCH) volatility process.
keywords:
Nonlinear asymmetric GARCH (NGARCH) volatility process.

The process of Engle and Ng [1]_, which is called NAGARCH in the rugarch
package for R.

Parameters
----------
p : int, optional
    Order of the symmetric innovation. Must satisfy p>=o and be positive.
o : int, optional
    Number of innovations that have a shift (an asymmetry parameter). Must
    satisfy o<=p and be non-negative. The first ``o`` of the ``p``
    innovations are shifted.
q : int, optional
    Order of the lagged conditional variance. Must be non-negative.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer.
ValueError
    If ``p`` is smaller than 1, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, or ``o`` is larger
    than ``p``.

Notes
-----
In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are

.. math::

    \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega
    +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}
    \left(\epsilon_{t-i}-\theta_{i}I_{[o\geq i]}\sigma_{t-i}\right)^{2}
    +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}\sigma_{t-j}^{2}

which is :math:`\sigma_{t-i}^2 (e_{t-i}-\theta_{i})^2` in terms of the
standardized shock :math:`e_{t}=\epsilon_{t}/\sigma_{t}`. The parameters are
named ``omega``, ``alpha[i]``, ``theta[i]`` and ``beta[j]``.

The shift :math:`\theta` is the position of the minimum of the news impact curve
in units of the lagged volatility. The sign convention is that of the rugarch
package and of most textbooks: a positive :math:`\theta` is the leverage effect,
since a negative shock then raises the variance more than a positive shock of
the same size. Engle and Ng [1]_ write the shift as
:math:`(\epsilon_{t-1}+\gamma\sigma_{t-1})^2` and expect :math:`\gamma<0`, so
that :math:`\theta=-\gamma`.

The name NGARCH is also used for the nonlinear ARCH model of Higgins and
Bera [2]_, which is a different model and is not available here.

The expected value of :math:`(e_{t}-\theta)^2` is :math:`1+\theta^2` for any
standardized distribution, since :math:`e_t` has mean 0 and variance 1. The
process is covariance stationary if the persistence

.. math::

    \phi=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\left(1+\theta_{i}^{2}\right)
    +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}

is smaller than 1, and then the unconditional variance of :math:`\epsilon_t` is
:math:`\omega/(1-\phi)`. Analytic forecasts are exact at every horizon. When
:math:`p=q=1`, they satisfy :math:`f_h=\omega+\phi f_{h-1}`.

Estimation uses the linear constraints :math:`\omega,\alpha_i,\beta_j\geq 0` and
:math:`\sum\alpha_i+\sum\beta_j<1`, as for :class:`~arch.univariate.APARCH`,
and bounds of -5 and 5 for :math:`\theta`. The stationarity condition
:math:`\phi<1` is not imposed during estimation, since it is not linear in the
parameters, and a model with :math:`\theta\neq 0` can be estimated with a
persistence of 1 or more. ``fit`` then issues a ``ValueWarning``.

With ``o=0`` there is no shift and the process is a GARCH process, so
:class:`~arch.univariate.GARCH` should be used instead. A ``ValueWarning`` is
issued in this case.

Before the start of the sample, the variance and the squared residual are both
replaced by the backcast of the variance, so that each shock term is
:math:`\alpha_i(1+\theta_i^2)` times the backcast.

References
----------
.. [1] Engle, R. F., & Ng, V. K. (1993). Measuring and testing the impact of
   news on volatility. *The Journal of Finance*, 48(5), 1749-1778.
.. [2] Higgins, M. L., & Bera, A. K. (1992). A class of nonlinear ARCH models.
   *International Economic Review*, 33(1), 137-158.

Parameters

tau0 : int or float, optional

ValueError

    ``tau0`` is not larger than ``tau1``, ``kmax`` is smaller than 1, ``rho`` is
    not larger than 1, or ``tau1 * rho ** (kmax - 1)`` is larger than ``tau0``.

Notes
-----
The variance dynamics of the model are given as a weighted average of kmax EWMA
variance processes where the smoothing parameters and weights are determined by
tau0, tau1 and rho.

This model has no parameters since the smoothing parameter is fixed.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.cutoff_to_index
entries.summary: Convert a cutoff to a numerical index.
keywords:
Convert a cutoff to a numerical index.

Parameters
----------
cutoff : int, str, date, datetime, datetime64, Timestamp, Period or None
    The cutoff point to use. An int is the location of the observation, and
    must be between -len(index) and len(index), inclusive. A negative int
    counts from the end, as in Python slicing, so that -1 is len(index) - 1
    and the result is never negative. Dates, strings and periods can only
    be used when index is a DatetimeIndex or a
    PeriodIndex, and must not be before the first or after the last date
    in index. A Period is converted to the first instant in the period.
index : Index
    Pandas index. Must be a DatetimeIndex or a PeriodIndex if cutoff is a
    date, a datetime, a datetime64, a Timestamp, a Period or a string.
default : int
    The value to return if cutoff is None. Must be between 0 and the length
    of index, inclusive.

Returns
-------
int
    The integer location of the cutoff, which is not negative.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If cutoff is not None, an integer or a date-like value, index is not an
    Index, or default is not an integer.
ValueError
    If default is an integer that is not between 0 and the length of index,
    cutoff is an integer that is not between -len(index) and len(index), or
    cutoff is a date-like value and the index is not a
    DatetimeIndex or a PeriodIndex, or the date is not within the index.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.date_to_index
entries.summary: Look up a date in an array of dates.
keywords:
Look up a date in an array of dates.

Parameters
----------
date : str, datetime, datetime64 or Timestamp
    Date to use when returning the index.
date_index : DatetimeIndex, Series or ndarray
    Index data containing datetime64 values.

Returns
-------
int
    Index location.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If date is not a str, a datetime, a datetime64 or a Timestamp, or
    date_index does not contain datetime64 values.
ValueError
    If date_index is empty, is not increasing and unique, or date is a str
    that cannot be parsed to a date.

Notes
-----
Assumes dates are increasing and unique. The result is the location of date
if it is in date_index, and otherwise the location where it would be
inserted: 0 for a date before the first date and the length of date_index
for a date after the last date. `cutoff_to_index` rejects the dates that
are not within the index.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.ensure1d
entries.summary: Convert data to a 1-d float64 ndarray or Series.
keywords:
Convert data to a 1-d float64 ndarray or Series.

Parameters
----------
x : array_like, Series or DataFrame
    The data to convert. A DataFrame must have a single column, and any
    other input must have at most one dimension with more than one element.
    Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to
    float64. float16 data are not accepted.
name : Hashable or None
    The name of the variable. Used in error messages and as the name of
    the Series if x is not a Series or a DataFrame and series is True.
series : bool, optional
    If True, return a Series. If False, return an ndarray.
allow_complex : bool, optional
    If True, complex data are converted to complex128 and real data to
    float64. If False, complex data are not accepted.

Returns
-------
ndarray or Series
    The 1-d data. A Series if series is True and an ndarray otherwise. The
    dtype is float64, or complex128 if allow_complex and x is complex. The
    index of a Series is kept. x is returned, or is a view of x, if x is
    float64 data (or complex128 data if allow_complex). The name of a Series
    that is not a str is converted to a str.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If x cannot be squeezed to 1 dimension.
TypeError
    If x cannot be converted to real float64 values (None cannot be
    converted), or to complex128 values if allow_complex, if x is float16 or
    complex data that are not allowed, name is not hashable or series is not
    a bool.

Notes
-----
x is never modified. NaN and inf are not checked, because the function
is used by code that handles them; the callers that need finite data
check it.

entries.name: arch.utility.cov.check_array
entries.summary: Convert array_like data to float64 and check its dimensions and values.
keywords:
Convert array_like data to float64 and check its dimensions and values.

This uses the conversion of `arch.utility.array.as_float64`, which ``ensure1d``
and ``ensure2d`` also use. The result is an ndarray. Call ``ensure1d`` or
``ensure2d`` first if the index of a pandas object must be kept, and use this
function for the checks.

Parameters
----------
name : str
    The name of the argument, which is used in the error message.
value : array_like, Series or DataFrame
    The data. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted
    to float64. float16 data are not accepted.
ndim : int, optional
    The number of dimensions of the result, 1 or 2. If ``squeeze`` is True, 1-d
    data can have any shape with a single dimension longer than 1 (a column, a row
    or a scalar) and 2-d data can be a scalar or 1-d (which becomes a column), as in
    ``ensure1d`` and ``ensure2d``.
shape : sequence of int or None, optional
    The required shape of the result. None in a position accepts any size. The
    length of the sequence is the number of dimensions, and it replaces ``ndim``.
min_length : int, optional
    The smallest accepted size of the first dimension.
squeeze : bool, optional
    If False, ``ndim`` (or ``len(shape)``) must be the number of dimensions of the
    data exactly, and nothing is reshaped.
allow_nan : bool, optional
    If True, NaN is accepted.
allow_inf : bool, optional
    If True, inf and -inf are accepted.
allow_none : bool, optional
    If True, None is accepted and returned unchanged.
allow_complex : bool, optional
    If True, complex data are converted to complex128, and real data to float64.
    If False, complex data are not accepted. NaN and inf are checked in the real
    and the imaginary part.

Returns
-------
ndarray or None
    The float64 data, or the complex128 data if ``allow_complex`` and the data are
    complex. This is ``value`` itself if it is a float64 ndarray (or complex128 if
    ``allow_complex``) with the required number of dimensions. None if
    ``allow_none`` and ``value`` is None.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If the data cannot be converted to float64 (strings, dates, objects that are
    not numbers, None), are float16, or are complex numbers and ``allow_complex``
    is False.
ValueError
    If the data do not have the required number of dimensions, shape or length, or
    contain NaN or inf where that is not allowed.

entries.name: arch.utility.cov.cov_nw
entries.summary: Compute the Newey-West covariance for 1-d and 2-d arrays.
keywords:
Compute the Newey-West covariance for 1-d and 2-d arrays.

Parameters
----------
y : array_like
    Values to use when computing the Newey-West covariance estimator, either
    1-d or 2-d. When y is 2d, default behavior is to treat columns as variables
    and rows as observations. Integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to
    float64, and complex data to complex128. float16 data are not accepted.
    Must not contain NaN or infinite values.
lags : int, optional
    Number of lags to include in the Newey-West covariance estimator. Must be
    non-negative and at most the number of observations.
demean : bool, optional
    Indicates whether to subtract the mean.
axis : int, optional
    The axis to use when y is 2d.
ddof : int, optional
    Degree of freedom correction for compatibility with simple covariance
    estimators. Must be non-negative and smaller than the number of
    observations.

Returns
-------
float or ndarray
    The estimated covariance. A float if y is 1-d and a 2-d ndarray
    otherwise. The covariance of complex data is Hermitian, so that it is
    real if y is 1-d and a complex128 matrix if y is 2-d.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If y cannot be converted to float64 or complex128 (it is float16, or
    contains strings or objects that are not numbers) or if lags, demean, axis
    or ddof have the wrong type. Booleans and floats are not accepted for the
    integers.
ValueError
    If y is not 1-d or 2-d, is empty or contains NaN or infinite values, or if
    lags, axis or ddof are outside their range.

Notes
-----
The covariance of complex data is the Hermitian covariance, which uses the
conjugate transpose: the term at lag j is the sum of z_t times the conjugate
of z_{t-j}, and a term and its conjugate transpose are added for each lag. It
is the covariance of the Bartlett kernel estimator in
:mod:`arch.covariance.kernel`. The pseudo-covariance is not estimated.

entries.name: arch.utility.timeseries.add_trend
entries.summary: Add a trend and/or constant to an array.
keywords:
Add a trend and/or constant to an array.

Parameters
----------
x : array_like or DataFrame, optional
    Original array of data. If None, then nobs must be a positive integer.
    Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to
    float64, and complex data to complex128. float16 data are not accepted.
    NaN and inf in x are not checked and are returned unchanged.
trend : {"n", "c", "t", "ct", "ctt"}, optional
    The trend(s) to add. Not case sensitive. Supported options are:

    * "n" no trend (no-op)
    * "c" add constant only
    * "t" add trend only
    * "ct" add constant and linear trend
    * "ctt" add constant and linear and quadratic trend.
prepend : bool, optional
    If True, prepends the new data to the columns of x.
nobs : int, optional
    Positive integer containing the length of the trend series. Must be
    None if x is provided.
has_constant : {"raise", "add", "skip"}, optional
    Controls what happens when trend is "c", "ct" or "ctt" and a constant
    already exists in x. "raise" will raise an error. "add" will duplicate a
    constant. "skip" will return the data without change. "skip" is the
    default. Not case sensitive.

Returns
-------
ndarray or DataFrame
    The trend if x is None, an ndarray with nobs rows. Otherwise x with the
    trend columns added, which is a DataFrame if x is a DataFrame and an
    ndarray otherwise. The trend columns of a DataFrame are named "const",
    "trend" and "quadratic_trend". The trend columns are real, and the data are
    complex128 if x is complex.

Raises
------
TypeError
    If trend or has_constant is not a str, prepend is not a bool, nobs is
    not an integer, or x cannot be converted to float64 or complex128 data
    (it is float16, or contains strings or objects that are not numbers).
ValueError
    If trend or has_constant is not one of the supported options, if both
    or neither of x and nobs are provided, if nobs is not positive, or if
    has_constant is "raise" and x already contains a constant.

Notes
-----
The columns of the trend are ordered constant, linear trend and quadratic
trend whenever applicable. There is currently no checking for an existing
trend.

keywords:
from arch.unitroot import ADF
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm
data = sm.datasets.macrodata.load().data

entries.name: arch/recipe/samplers-python
entries.summary: samplers python
keywords:
from arch.compat.numba import jit

from arch._typing import Float64Array, Int64Array


def stationary_bootstrap_sample_python(
    indices: Int64Array, u: Float64Array, p: float
) -> Int64Array:
    """
    Generate indices for sampling from the stationary bootstrap.

    Parameters
    -------
    indices: ndarray
        Single-dimensional array containing draws from randint with the same
        size as the data in the range of [0,nobs).
    u : ndarray
        Single-dimensional Array of standard uniforms.
    p : float
        Probability that a new block is started in the stationary bootstrap.
        The multiplicative reciprocal of the window length.

    Returns
    -------
    ndarray
        Indices for an iteration of the stationary bootstrap.
    """
    num_items = indices.shape[0]
    for i in range(1, num_items):
        if u[i] > p:
            indices[i] = indices[i - 1] + 1
            if indices[i] == num_items:
                indices[i] = 0

    return indices


stationary_bootstrap_sample = jit(stationary_bootstrap_sample_python)
